suggestion.title: Chrome Extension Install – Suspicious Metadata or Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Article states extension was 'malicious Perplexity Chrome Extension,' implying installation via deception (typosquatting, lookalike branding). No UC captures extension installation anomalies or manifest inspection. Expected: monitor for extension installs with suspicious names, icons, or descriptions mimicking legitimate vendors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome process creation of install events or registry/filesystem writes to Extensions folders. Flag installs from non-gallery sources, installs with names containing common typos (e.g., 'Perplex' instead of 'Perplexity'), or installs triggering no browser UI approval. Cross-reference extension ID and manifest hash against threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Search Query Exfiltration – Unusual Chrome Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'intercepted searches and address bar input'; this implies collection + exfiltration. Pipeline has no UC for detecting outbound connections from chrome.exe to attacker C&C or suspicious data-encoding patterns in HTTP/HTTPS traffic from browser processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag chrome.exe initiating connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains, especially high-frequency beaconing patterns. Monitor for POST requests with encoded payloads (base64, hex) from browser process to non-whitelisted destinations. Correlate with search-heavy user sessions (high browser CPU/memory) + unexpected egress.

suggestion.title: Browser Input Capture – Content Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'intercepted searches and address bar input,' indicating content scripts hooking into search forms and omnibox. No UC addresses dynamic script injection, content script registration, or hooking of sensitive input handlers (search boxes, password fields, address bars).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect content scripts registered to intercept input on common search engines (google.com, bing.com, perplexity.com). Monitor for DOM mutation observers targeting input elements or keyboard event listeners added by untrusted scripts. Flag extensions with permissions for all URLs (`<all_urls>`) combined with network access permissions.

suggestion.title: Extension Privilege Escalation – Unrequested Permissions or Silent Updates
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious extension capturing sensitive input; pipeline has no UC for detecting extension permission escalation, silent manifest updates, or code injection post-installation. Expected: monitor for extensions requesting excessive permissions or permissions changing without user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag extensions modifying their manifest.json to add new permissions after initial install. Monitor for chrome.exe spawning unusual child processes or injecting code into renderer processes. Detect extensions persisting via startup folders, registry Run keys, or scheduled tasks (extension auto-launch).

suggestion.title: Address Bar / Omnibox Monitoring – Keystroke Capture Evidence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Address Bar Input' was intercepted. Pipeline missed detection scenario for hooking omnibox keystroke events or logging typed URLs before submission, which precedes exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extension code registering listeners on chrome.omnibox.onInputChanged or onInputEntered events. Detect unusual string patterns in extension background script logs matching URL prefixes or common credential formats (http://, https://, email patterns). Correlate with search interception to confirm dual-collection malware.

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension Distribution – Chrome Web Store or Lookalike Repo
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies the extension existed in some form available for installation (official store, sideload, or phishing link). Pipeline has no IOC or UC for tracking distribution infrastructure, download hashes, or store page indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed/successful extension downloads with source domain reputation. Flag downloads from non-official Chrome Web Store mirrors or direct .crx file URLs from suspicious domains. Monitor for extension store page clones (lookalike domains). Hash malicious extension .crx file and distribute to EDR as known-bad indicator.

suggestion.title: AI Browser Prompt Injection Credential Leak Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'tricks AI browsers into leaking credentials'—implies prompt injection or manipulation of AI-assisted parsing to extract sensitive data. No use cases generated despite this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal prompt injection payloads in browser logs, AI feature query strings, or local storage that contain credential-extraction keywords. Flag AI browser features spawning child processes or making unexpected outbound connections to credential vaults or external exfil endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI Agent Credential Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets credential leakage via AI browser—implies unauthorized access to password managers, session tokens, or authentication secrets. Title states 'leaking user credentials' but pipeline failed to map credential_access techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AI browser processes or threads accessing credential storage locations (DPAPI, keychain, password manager DBs). Alert on unusual pattern: legitimate user session → AI feature invocation → credential store access outside normal browser operation.

suggestion.title: BioShocking Campaign Attribution & Indicator Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article title names the attack 'BioShocking' but pipeline produced zero IOCs, campaign identifiers, or threat-actor attribution. This named attack should be tracked as a campaign indicator across mail, web, DNS, and endpoint telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish a detection baseline for emails, URLs, payloads, or process names containing 'BioShocking' as an attack signature. Track domains and IP infrastructure linked to distribution. Monitor for credential-phishing emails targeting AI-browser-using organizations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI Feature Access for Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Attack specifically exploits AI browser features—suggests misuse of legitimate AI assistants or agents. Pipeline should have identified this execution vector and mapped it to defense-evasion and exfiltration techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credentials or sensitive data passed as arguments to AI browser processes or AI API calls. Alert on unusual data volume exfiltrated through AI-assisted chat or command channels. Flag credential strings in outbound network traffic initiated by browser AI features.

suggestion.title: WebKit Remote Code Execution via Malicious Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'WebKit Bugs' patched in this release. WebKit is the browser engine for Safari and iOS browsers; RCE via malicious web content is the canonical attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Safari or WebKit rendering engine spawning system processes, elevated code execution from browser contexts, or unexpected IPC to kernel components during web navigation.

suggestion.title: iOS Sandbox Escape Post-Browser Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions iOS flaws; WebKit sandbox is a primary security boundary in iOS. Patch notes typically include sandbox escape CVEs exploitable after initial browser RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sandboxed app processes acquiring entitlements (Bluetooth, Location, Camera, sensitive files) without user authorization, or unprivileged processes spawning privileged children post-compromise.

suggestion.title: macOS Local Privilege Escalation via Kernel/System Service Flaw
suggestion.rationale: macOS is explicitly mentioned in scope. Apple security advisories routinely include kernel, IOKit, or system daemon vulnerabilities enabling local privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged user processes attempting Mach RPC to privileged daemons, spawning children with SUID escalation, or accessing protected kernel memory regions.

suggestion.title: Browser-to-OS Exploit Chain via Process Injection or Memory Corruption
suggestion.rationale: Batch patch article listing 30+ flaws; typical chains exploit browser vulnerabilities to gain code execution, then pivot via kernel bugs (injection or memory corruption) to full system access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect code injection into Safari, reverse IPC from browser to system services, unsigned binary execution from browser process memory, or abnormal writable regions in kernel-critical processes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Device Detection: Unpatched iOS/macOS Post-Advisory
suggestion.rationale: Article patch release date marks onset of attack surface; devices failing to patch within SLA window remain exploitable for known CVEs in this batch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on devices running pre-patch iOS/macOS versions 72+ hours post-advisory, automatic security updates disabled, or failed update attempts on high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Browser Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious Perplexity Chrome extension'—a persistence mechanism. Pipeline missed extension installation/registry activity detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation of Chrome/Edge extensions with names spoofing legitimate services (e.g., Perplexity-like variants) or from unverified publishers. Monitor extension directories and registry keys for unsigned or obfuscated manifest metadata.

suggestion.title: Search Query and Address Bar Input Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title states extension 'intercepted searches and address bar input'—direct data collection attack. Pipeline missed T1056.004 and exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes initiating connections to C2 infrastructure with serialized browser history, search terms, or navigation URLs in POST payloads. Correlate extension process tree to validate data source originates from extension context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted for command-and-control infrastructure. Article implies C2 to exfiltrate intercepted user input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS/HTTP connections from browser extension processes to newly-registered domains, privacy-protected registrations, or low-reputation ASNs. Baseline against known Perplexity official infrastructure to exclude false positives.

suggestion.title: Browser Extension Permission Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Intercepting address bar and search requires <all_urls> or tabs permission. Article mentions interception capability but pipeline missed permission-audit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Chrome/Edge extension installations requesting webRequest, debugger, or <all_urls> host permissions. Cross-reference stated extension purpose (e.g., productivity tool) against permission scope—scope creep indicates potential malware.

suggestion.title: Credential/Browsing History Interception via Malicious Extension
suggestion.rationale: Address bar input may include credentials, URLs with sensitive parameters. Pipeline failed to model credential-access risk from extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser extension outbound traffic for high-entropy or base64-encoded payloads resembling serialized credential material or sensitive URLs. Alert on extensions with keyboard-hook or form-capture capability.

suggestion.title: Counterfeit Browser Extension Installation from Unofficial Source
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension impersonated legitimate Perplexity service. Pipeline did not identify typosquatting or publisher-verification gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed extensions against official provider lists. Alert on installations of similarly-named extensions from non-official publishers or with metadata mismatches (icon, permissions, review count) relative to canonical versions.

suggestion.title: SimpleHelp RMM CVE-2026-48558 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Attackers Exploit SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558' — this is the initial compromise vector and should trigger alerts on SimpleHelp access anomalies, authentication abuse, or known exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal SimpleHelp process execution, failed and successful authentication attempts to SimpleHelp services, and any POST requests to known vulnerable SimpleHelp endpoints. Flag unusual child processes spawned by SimpleHelp (simhelp.exe, shjwmain.exe) with obfuscated command lines.

suggestion.title: TaskWeaver Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware was deployed 'to Deploy TaskWeaver' — needs detection for TaskWeaver process creation, file writes, and behavioral indicators post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TaskWeaver process creation or known file hashes. Monitor for unsigned binaries or scripts executing from temporary directories post-SimpleHelp exploitation. Look for TaskWeaver command-line arguments, registry modifications, or DLL injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Djinn Stealer Credential Harvesting Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Djinn Stealer' by name — stealer malware typically targets credentials from browsers, password managers, and local stores; should detect anomalous credential access and memory dumping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Djinn Stealer process creation by hash/name. Monitor for credential access to browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe), LSA process access (lsass.exe), and reads from common password store locations (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, .ssh directories, browser credential stores).

suggestion.title: Djinn Stealer Data Exfiltration to C2
suggestion.rationale: Stealer functionality implies exfiltration ('Djinn Stealer'); article suggests data theft is a primary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections from TaskWeaver or Djinn Stealer processes to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure. Alert on exfiltration volume anomalies and encrypted data transfers to external IPs shortly after malware execution.

suggestion.title: Persistence via SimpleHelp RMM Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RMM tools like SimpleHelp provide built-in persistence; after gaining access via CVE-2026-48558, attackers can establish long-term presence via remote sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual SimpleHelp remote sessions initiated from external or suspicious IPs. Alert on non-business-hours SimpleHelp RMM activity, multiple failed authentication attempts followed by success, or SimpleHelp spawning unusual child processes.

suggestion.title: Malware Deployment via Legitimate RMM Child Process
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploitation enables arbitrary code execution; article implies TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer are deployed as secondary payloads through SimpleHelp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned by SimpleHelp (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, wmic.exe). Flag any SimpleHelp process writing executables or scripts to disk, particularly in temp directories or with double extensions.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Launch with Remote Debugging Port
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism explicitly described: 'connect to the browser's management console in headless mode via a remote debugging port' and 'launch the browser, connect via the remote debugging port to take control.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Chromium-based browser processes (chrome.exe, edge.exe, chromium.exe) spawned with --remote-debugging-port flag, especially in headless mode or from non-user-interactive contexts. Flag DLL sideloading precursors (rundll32, regsvcs launching browser).

suggestion.title: OAuth Authorization Code Theft via Google API
suggestion.rationale: Direct credential theft mechanism: 'they obtained an OAuth authorization code, which they subsequently exchanged for an access token to reach the target resources via the API.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth authorization code requests and token exchanges initiated from non-interactive processes, command-line tools, or APIs. Correlate token acquisitions with browser debugging sessions or abnormal user-agent strings.

suggestion.title: Headless Browser Execution for Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Defense evasion vector: 'launch the browser in headless mode' to execute browser operations without visible window, bypassing user-facing security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes with --headless command-line argument, especially when combined with --disable-background-networking, --disable-sync, or when spawned from rundll32/regsvcs proxies or temporary directories.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading for Umbrij Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Tag keywords 'DLL sideloading' indicate ToddyCat TTP; Umbrij tool likely deployed via DLL search order hijacking to evade direct executable detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate Windows binaries (rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, regasm.exe, msiexec.exe) loading DLLs from writable paths, temp directories, or with mismatched names. Correlate DLL loads with subsequent browser spawning or network traffic to Google APIs.

suggestion.title: Gmail API Bulk Access from Non-Standard Client
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration phase: 'access to the victim's cloud account via the Google API' and 'access to Google account resources within the context of the user's saved session' from automated tool context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gmail API methods (messages.list, messages.get, threads.list) executed in bulk from non-standard user agents or IP addresses. Flag rapid sequential email access (>100 messages/min) in short timeframes from automated processes.

suggestion.title: Umbrij Malware Process Execution and Variants
suggestion.rationale: Named malware tool: 'threat actors developed a tool called Umbrij' and later 'discovered several versions of the Umbrij tool.' Direct detection of tool instantiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes named 'Umbrij', 'umbrij.exe', or file paths containing 'umbrij'. Cross-correlate with DLL sideloading events, browser debugging flags, or Google API requests in process command lines.

suggestion.title: Repeated AirDrop/Quick Share Connection Attempts from Single Proximity Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'nearby attackers trigger crashes'—prerequisite is sending multiple crafted packets. Detect sustained connection attempts from single Bluetooth MAC within proximity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 AirDrop or Quick Share connection attempts from same external Bluetooth MAC address in <2 minute window, especially if followed by target device application crash or service restart.

suggestion.title: Malformed File-Transfer Packet Causing Service Crash
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: crafted packets trigger crashes. Correlate malformed AirDrop/Quick Share traffic with application termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag application crash (sharingd, com.google.android.gms) within 30 seconds of receiving truncated, oversized, or malformed AirDrop/Quick Share protocol frame from unauthenticated source.

suggestion.title: Security Check Bypass in File Transfer Acceptance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions bypass of checks. Detect transfers that succeed without proper authentication or consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify AirDrop/Quick Share file transfers accepted without user interaction or with spoofed sender identity (device name mismatch, invalid UDID, missing TLS handshake).

suggestion.title: Bluetooth Service Enumeration Targeting AirDrop UUIDs
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must first discover vulnerable AirDrop/Quick Share services. Detect unusual GATT discovery from untrusted Bluetooth peers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated attempts to enumerate specific Apple AirDrop Bluetooth service UUIDs (e.g., C1E24DC4-5EC3-4B7F-A0E7-8B9C4D8C8C8C) or Google Quick Share service handles from external Bluetooth MAC.

suggestion.title: LoadMaster Pre-Auth RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Run Root Commands Pre-Auth'—core indicator of unauthenticated endpoint leading to arbitrary command execution. Pipeline missed the entire initial access/execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LoadMaster administrative endpoints for requests without valid authentication tokens, followed by abnormal HTTP response codes or shell metacharacters in request bodies. Correlate with root process spawning events to confirm exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Root Command Execution via LoadMaster Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes 'root commands'—privilege escalation from web application context to system-level execution. No UC generated for this critical post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell process creation (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, sh.exe) spawned by LoadMaster process with UID 0 (root). Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP requests to the management interface or API endpoints with encoding anomalies.

suggestion.title: LoadMaster Vulnerable Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Pre-auth RCE implies a specific vulnerable endpoint. Pipeline should detect reconnaissance for version identification and endpoint discovery before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known LoadMaster diagnostic or backup endpoints (/diag, /backup, /api/version) without authentication credentials. Watch for 404 patterns followed by successful access—may indicate version probing before targeted exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence Installation via LoadMaster
suggestion.rationale: Critical severity RCE with root access enables full compromise. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for persistence mechanisms installed by root-level process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron jobs, systemd timers, or SSH public key installations created under /root or /etc/cron.d following LoadMaster process execution. Flag modification of LoadMaster configuration files with content changes inconsistent with legitimate administration.

suggestion.title: LoadMaster Web Server Request Anomaly Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires crafted HTTP request to trigger RCE. Pipeline should detect payload patterns indicative of exploitation attempts (shell metacharacters, command separators).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to LoadMaster endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $(), backticks), common web exploit patterns (../../, null bytes), or base64-encoded payloads in query parameters or POST bodies from non-authenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: WebKit Memory Corruption Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites '30+ iOS, macOS, Safari Flaws, Including AI-Discovered WebKit Bugs'—these are typically memory-safety defects (use-after-free, integer overflow, buffer overflow) enabling arbitrary code execution via malicious web content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Safari process crashes with abnormal exit codes (0xc0000374, EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION) or EDR memory violations immediately before child process spawn. Baseline crash patterns pre-patch and alert on deviation post-patch to catch both exploitation and regression.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Apple Device Exposure Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multiple iOS and macOS security patches released. Detection pipeline should identify systems running vulnerable versions to measure Time-to-Patch and exposure window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query device inventory for OS versions predating patch release date. Correlate patch publication date with fleet-wide patch adoption. Alert on devices still running vulnerable iOS/macOS versions 7+ days post-patch availability.

suggestion.title: Malicious Content Delivery to Vulnerable Browsers
suggestion.rationale: WebKit 0-day-adjacent bugs (described as 'AI-Discovered') are high-value targets for exploit kits and drive-by download campaigns serving malicious payloads to unpatched Safari instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Safari connections to known malware hosters, exploit-kit staging sites, or suspicious redirects (legitimate domain→attacker infrastructure). Flag redirect chains during Safari sessions. Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript or inline exploit payloads in HTTP responses.

suggestion.title: Browser-Based Memory Disclosure Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Memory corruption bugs often require heap spraying or memory layout disclosure to reliably exploit. Look for abnormal memory access patterns or large allocations preceding crash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large or repeated allocations in Safari memory space (heap spray indicators), unusual mmap/mprotect syscalls, or syscalls to read /proc/self/maps. Correlate with subsequent memory access violations.

suggestion.title: Exploit Kit Forensic Footprint: WebKit-Specific Signals
suggestion.rationale: AI-discovered bugs likely exploited via automated exploit generation, not manual exploitation. Detection should capture novel or atypical exploitation patterns not present in known CVE exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Safari crashes in uncommon call stacks, at unusual heap offsets, or with ROP/JOP gadget signatures inconsistent with public Safari exploits. Monitor for injection into Safari child processes (content processes, GPU processes) following WebKit crashes.

suggestion.title: Critical Patch Compliance Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes '30+ flaws' patched in critical platforms (iOS, macOS, Safari). Detection should enforce patch deployment within SLA and surface non-compliant devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track devices by patch deployment date. Alert on any device not reaching patched OS version within 72 hours of release for critical Apple security updates. Correlate with device risk score and network criticality.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero UCs. This is the core attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated HTTP/TCP access to Splunk Enterprise instances on PostgreSQL sidecar service ports (typically 8191). Alert on connection attempts to `<splunk-instance>:*/sidecar/postgres*` endpoints from external/untrusted networks with no prior authentication token.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Creation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No UC captures file-system modification signature of this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/truncation operations originating from Splunk Enterprise service processes (splunkd, sidecar) when triggered by external HTTP requests to unauthenticated endpoints. Flag rapid or sequential file operations in sensitive directories (logs, configs, application roots).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Splunk Enterprise Public-Facing Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE applies to exposed assets and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline provided no such UC. Splunk Enterprise instances exposed to internet are exploitable via T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances reachable on standard web ports (8000, 8089, 8191) from external networks. Cross-reference against patch inventory for CVE-2026-20253 remediation status. Alert on any unpatched instances receiving inbound traffic from untrusted IP ranges.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Anomalous Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit vector as 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline missed detection of abnormal access to this service component. Legitimate traffic should be from Splunk control plane only.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate PostgreSQL sidecar connections (source IPs, ports, request patterns). Alert on requests from non-Splunk infrastructure, requests without authentication headers, requests originating from external/untrusted networks, or anomalously large payloads in file creation requests.

suggestion.title: File Truncation for Log Manipulation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker capability: 'truncate arbitrary files.' This is a secondary impact worth hunting as defensive evasion after initial access gain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected file truncation events (zero-byte rewrites) targeting log files, audit trails, or configuration files on Splunk-hosting systems. Correlate timing of truncations with prior unauthenticated access attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar. Flag truncations originating from sidecar service processes as anomalous.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit the sidecar endpoint — requires detection of connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar (typically port 5432 variant) without authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated connections to Splunk Enterprise hosts on PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or documented sidecar port). Alert if connection succeeds without prior PostgreSQL authentication credentials. Correlate with public Splunk exposure via port scans or shodan queries.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create... arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires file-write monitoring from PostgreSQL process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation initiated by postgresql.exe or sidecar service process writing to unexpected directories (outside /var/lib/postgresql or configured data paths). Particularly sensitive to paths outside Splunk's install directory or to system-critical locations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'truncate arbitrary files' — distinct detection from creation, focusing on file-deletion or zeroing operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation or deletion operations (SetEndOfFile, DeleteFile) originating from postgresql process or Splunk sidecar service. Baseline acceptable truncation (e.g., log rotation); flag truncation of configuration, state, or security-relevant files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article references standard asset-exposure hunt template and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — requires inventory and exposure scanning for unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise assets via internal asset inventory, port scans (8000, 9998, sidecar ports), or product telemetry. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Flag assets with exposed sidecar endpoints accessible from untrusted networks. Federal due date: 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the core attack vector and warrants detection of auth-bypass or unauthenticated connection attempts to the sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service logs for connection attempts without valid authentication. Alert on successful or failed authentication-bypass attempts, especially from external network ranges. Correlate timing with CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scanner alerts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Context
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—monitor Splunk file-system events for unauthorized file operations via the sidecar service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file creation or deletion in Splunk directories when initiated from PostgreSQL sidecar service context. Alert on modifications to Splunk config, var, or auth directories without corresponding change tickets. Include baseline of legitimate sidecar file operations to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service on Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires network-reachable 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—assets exposed on public/DMZ networks with unpatched versions represent immediate attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset-exposure hunt: identify Splunk Enterprise instances with PostgreSQL sidecar ports (default 5432 or org-specific) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-20253. Escalate any unpatched instances visible from internet-facing segments or untrusted VLANs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status and Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE explicitly identified in CISA KEV as actively exploited; article includes federal patch due date (2026-06-21)—standard vulnerability scanning for this CVE should be a primary indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any scanner detection of CVE-2026-20253 affecting Splunk Enterprise. Prioritize findings by network exposure and patch lag. Flag instances approaching federal due date without confirmed remediation. Recommend immediate patching for all vulnerable instances in production.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline generated zero use cases. T1190 implies internet-facing instances at risk. Must detect exposed Splunk Enterprise on port 8000 or 8089 accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (banner grab, port scanning, certificate enumeration) reachable from external IP space. Correlate with patch inventory for CVE-2026-20253 status. Flag unpatched instances with internet routes as critical priority.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline missed endpoint-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/network requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (Splunk services) originating from external networks. Flag requests without valid authentication tokens/sessions that receive HTTP 200–204 responses. Alert on POST/DELETE methods to file-management endpoints.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for this post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file creation or truncation on Splunk Enterprise servers (especially in /opt/splunk/etc, config directories). Correlate filesystem events with access logs showing unauthenticated or sidecar endpoint requests. Flag suspicious file paths (traversal sequences, config overwrites).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Detection (Critical Function Access)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function.' Article: vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated user.' Pipeline did not model this bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful API/endpoint access to Splunk's sensitive functions (file services, config services) when authentication headers are missing, invalid, or empty. Baseline: 100% of legitimate requests carry valid session/auth tokens. Flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Service Disruption via Malicious File Truncation

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Splunk application logs for unauthenticated requests to critical endpoints (file operations, configuration management, search functions). Cross-correlate with authentication system logs to identify any enforcement gaps on high-privilege functions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Sidecar Service Unexpected Schema Changes
suggestion.rationale: 'Create or truncate arbitrary files' via PostgreSQL sidecar implies potential data manipulation. Article describes a critical-function bypass with file-level impact—database or config tampering.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Service Endpoint Taking Unauthenticated Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' access to 'critical function'—implies bypass of auth middleware. No UC checks service endpoint availability or auth-requirement flags.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized cross-user flow access — user accessing flow owned by different user
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows an authenticated attacker to execute any flow belonging to another user by specifying the victim's flow ID.' No UC explicitly detects the core exploit: a requester accessing a flow where their user_id ≠ flow.owner_id. This is the definitive attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate flow ownership metadata (from Langflow audit logs or API schema) with POST/GET requests to `/api/v1/responses`. Alert when a user token/session accesses a flow ID owned by a different user. Baseline: one user should only access their own flows except in documented admin/share scenarios.

suggestion.title: Sequential or predictable flow ID enumeration — attacker systematically testing flow IDs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes IDOR via 'specifying the victim's flow ID.' If flow IDs are sequential or predictable (UUIDs with low entropy), attackers enumerate them. Article implies this is the mechanism but no UC detects the enumeration pattern itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to `/api/v1/responses` with sequential, incrementing, or low-entropy flow IDs. Flag 404/403 responses (indicating non-existent or unauthorized flows) followed by successful 200 responses (indicating a valid flow was found). Baseline: typical users access a stable set of flows, not enumerate across ID ranges.

suggestion.title: Flow execution by non-owner — attacker executing victim's flow and collecting responses
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'execute any flow' and likely access outputs. This post-exploitation activity (exfiltration of flow results/responses) has no detection UC. Focus on execution + response retrieval patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to `/api/v1/responses` followed immediately by GET requests for response data, where the requester's user != flow owner. Correlate execution timestamp with response-fetch timestamp (should occur within seconds if attacker is harvesting outputs). Establish baseline of typical response-retrieval patterns per user.

suggestion.title: Authenticated user with unusual service-account behavior — new user making flow API calls
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated attacker,' implying use of a compromised account or newly-provisioned token. No UC detects behavioral anomalies in newly-active authentication principals calling the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Web requests to `/api/v1/responses` with first-time authentications or users with no prior API activity. Flag users or service accounts that transition from zero Langflow API activity to high-volume endpoint access within a narrow time window. Baseline: users who call Langflow APIs should have established patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk flow ID harvesting — attacker discovers all available flow IDs prior to exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker 'specifies the victim's flow ID,' but obtaining that ID requires prior reconnaissance. No UC covers the discovery phase where attacker enumerates all available flow IDs (e.g., via predictable ID patterns or directory traversal).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GET or HEAD requests to `/api/v1/responses` or similar enumeration endpoints with rapid iteration over ID ranges. Track 200 vs. 404 response patterns indicating an attacker testing IDs. Correlate with lack of subsequent write activity (i.e., reconnaissance without exploitation) to detect early-stage recon.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated Endpoint Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—explicit unauthenticated access vector requiring exposure hunt against Splunk service ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for successful HTTP connections to Splunk service endpoints (ports 8000, 8089) from external/untrusted sources that complete without authentication. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner data for instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Focus on unauthenticated POST/PUT requests to critical endpoints.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the exploitation vector; requires direct monitoring of sidecar process and network access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to Splunk sidecar service ports (PostgreSQL 5432 or Splunk ephemeral sidecar ports) originating from unexpected processes or remote sources. Alert on queries or commands to sidecar that bypass Splunk's authentication layer. Correlate with Splunk audit logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—requires detection of file system operations outside expected Splunk data directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk service process (splunkd.exe / splunkd) performing file writes, deletes, or truncations outside /opt/splunk/var/* or expected application directories. Flag modifications to /etc, /var/log, or system configuration paths. Monitor for rapid sequential file truncations suggesting deliberate data destruction.

suggestion.title: Scanner-Artifact Validation for CVE-2026-20253

Identify instances marked 'patched' running versions that fall within CVE-2026-20253 vulnerable ranges. Manually verify patches against official Splunk advisory; prioritize instances exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Instability Following Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: File truncation/creation attacks on service-critical files may trigger service crashes or abnormal restarts; implicit indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Splunk service (splunkd) unexpected restarts, crashes, or error states following any successful unauthenticated endpoint access event. Alert on repeated process spawning or resource exhaustion from sidecar service. Correlate service interruptions with file modification telemetry.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint

suggestion.title: Splunk File System Modifications Without Corresponding Auth Audit

suggestion.title: Inbound Network Connections to Splunk Sidecar from External IP Space

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access

suggestion.title: Craft CMS Host/X-Forwarded-Host header poisoning attempts

suggestion.title: JavaScript injection via baseUrl manipulation in Craft CMS responses

suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Blind SSRF' vulnerability but UC_102_3 only monitors outbound IP traffic.
