suggestion.rationale: Root cause of vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'; detecting systems with authentication disabled on sidecar endpoints is a preventive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Splunk configurations to identify instances where PostgreSQL sidecar authentication is not enforced (e.g., trust-based auth, no password set, IP restrictions absent). Flag production systems with sidecar endpoints accessible without credentials. Use baseline configuration snapshots to detect unauthorized relaxation of authentication policies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from PostgreSQL Sidecar Context
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation likely involves sidecar executing attacker commands or unusual file operations; detecting child process spawning from sidecar is an execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar process for spawning shell interpreters, scripting engines, or file manipulation utilities not normally associated with sidecar operation. Flag execution of binaries outside Splunk installation paths initiated from sidecar context. Alert on any shell invocation (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, powershell) from the sidecar process.

suggestion.title: OpenRemote authenticated user deleting alarms outside assigned realm (IDOR privilege escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms'—this is explicit privilege escalation. Pipeline UCs focus on volume/probing but miss the core escalation step of a low-privilege user accessing high-privilege targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful alarm DELETE requests with realm ACL or user provisioning data. Flag deletions where authenticated user lacks explicit access to target realm. Combine with historical baseline of per-user realm-access patterns.

suggestion.title: OpenRemote removeAlarms method invoked with cross-tenant alarm IDs (IDOR method exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes vulnerability in 'bulk removeAlarms() method'—detects the method invocation itself with out-of-scope alarm IDs, not just HTTP verbs. Pipeline UCs only track DELETE HTTP traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for removeAlarms() or similar bulk deletion method calls with alarm ID arrays. Extract alarm realm identifiers from payloads and cross-reference with invoking user's assigned realms. Flag mismatches.

suggestion.title: OpenRemote bulk alarm deletion by non-administrative service account (scope escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires only authentication, not admin role. Pipeline misses lateral-movement scenario where attacker steals service-account credentials and uses IDOR to delete cross-realm alarms en masse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service/bot account logins followed immediately by bulk DELETE requests. Compare volume and realm scope of service-account deletions to historical baselines; flag anomalous cross-realm deletions from non-human accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' with no authentication barrier. Zero use cases generated despite this being the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk ports (8000, 8089) lacking valid session tokens or Authorization headers. Baseline expected API paths; alert on requests to service endpoints returning 401/403, especially when followed by file operations from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' No post-exploitation file-operation detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track file create/write/delete events from Splunk service accounts (user 'splunk', postgres container processes) targeting locations outside Splunk home—/etc, /var, system config directories. Flag rapid truncation of existing files or file creation with non-standard names in protected paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Asset Inventory and Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch deadline 2026-06-21 requires scanner-based detection. Article provides no asset-exposure or vulnerability-scanner signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference scanner patch-version assertions against actual running version. Correlate with network exposure (8000/8089 accessible from untrusted networks) and patching logs to identify remediation lag.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is exploitable 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' without authentication. Pipeline generated no detection for this specific access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or service-specific) for connection attempts without valid authentication tokens or TLS client certificates. Flag any non-internal, unauthenticated sessions; correlate with Splunk Enterprise process and version to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk API
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files' via the vulnerable endpoint. Pipeline missed this file-manipulation detection entirely—a core impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation/truncation events (DeviceFileEvents) with Splunk Enterprise process lineage or API access logs. Alert on files created or truncated in unexpected directories (e.g., /etc, C:\Windows, application config paths) initiated by or attributed to Splunk service account or unauthenticated web requests.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure (Asset Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation against 'exposed assets.' Article does not mention internal-only deployments. Pipeline referenced a template but produced no concrete asset-hunt use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Splunk Enterprise listening on public IPs or accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20253. Check web proxy logs for Splunk authentication endpoints accessed from non-corporate ASNs or high-risk geographies.

suggestion.title: Failed vs. Successful Authentication to Critical Splunk Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline should surface auth bypass attempts—both failed auth checks and successful unauthenticated function invocations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk critical endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*) that lack authorization headers, return 200-class responses without prior login, or show mismatched user context. Correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar logs if available.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk REST API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files'; detection should cover REST calls without auth headers to Splunk /services endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST/PUT requests to Splunk /services/... endpoints originating from untrusted networks or with missing/invalid Authorization headers. Correlate with subsequent file-write or file-delete operations on the Splunk host to confirm exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability vector is 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; attackers will target this exposed endpoint directly
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically non-standard port or path) with file-operation payloads (CREATE, TRUNCATE). Alert on any sidecar hits from external IPs or without valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'truncate arbitrary files' as core impact; file-system level detection complements API-level hunts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file truncation or deletion events in Splunk directories (bin/, etc/, var/) or critical application paths when Splunk processes are not performing scheduled maintenance. Correlate with Splunk log entries showing API activity from untrusted sources in the same window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Exposure Hunt (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' via template; SOC must confirm no externally-reachable Splunk instances vulnerable to unauthenticated access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run network scan to identify Splunk Enterprise instances listening on public IPs (default port 8000, 9998, or custom). Attempt unauthenticated connection to /services/server/info endpoint; if accessible without credentials, flag as exploitable per CVE-2026-20253 and remediate by patch due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or Data File Modifications Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker truncates files via sidecar, Splunk behavior will degrade; detection should catch resulting anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk internal logs for repeated file-access errors, missing configuration errors, or startup failures following suspicious external API activity. Cross-reference with filesystem logs showing unexpected truncation events in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can access 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—must detect unauthorized endpoint access attempts to intercept initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on external or unauthenticated HTTP POST/PUT requests to Splunk sidecar service ports. Monitor for requests lacking valid authentication headers/tokens arriving from unexpected network ranges to internal Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files' through sidecar endpoint access—file-integrity monitoring must detect unauthorized file operations by Splunk processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Splunk processes (splunkd, python interpreters running Splunk code) creating or modifying files outside configured data/log directories. Correlate with sidecar endpoint access logs for stronger detection signal.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Database Operation Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service'—database audit logs should expose abnormal file or database operations initiated through the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs for file system operations or truncation commands initiated from sidecar processes lacking corresponding authenticated Splunk UI or API sessions. Flag database operations from unauthenticated service connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated no detection for this authentication bypass vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/TCP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically port 5432 or internal service port) without valid authentication headers or from non-Splunk infrastructure IPs. Flag requests containing PostgreSQL protocol handshakes or 'CREATE TABLE' / 'TRUNCATE' statements on the sidecar interface.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the exploitation primitive. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection for the actual file-system abuse that follows authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk process (splunkd, postgres) for unusual file operations: creation of files outside normal data/config directories, truncation of critical logs or config files, writes to sensitive paths (/etc, /var/log). Correlate with failed or anomalous network connections to PostgreSQL sidecar.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry ('observed exploited in the wild'), warranting direct IOC-based detection. Pipeline provided zero IOCs and no exploitation signature detection despite active threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index all Splunk and proxy logs for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signatures: requests to known vulnerable PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints, payloads containing file-operation commands, or access patterns matching public PoC code (if available). Cross-reference against patch status from vulnerability scanner.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—core exploitation path not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk processes or PostgreSQL services for file creation/truncation operations initiated from unauthenticated network contexts or lacking expected authentication tokens/headers. Alert on high-volume file truncation especially targeting config or system files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Sidecar Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20253 with technical vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero detections for this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (port inference from vulnerability details) lacking authentication headers or tokens. Cross-reference against known Splunk service ports and sidecar endpoint patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Exposure & Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets; article references 'public-facing application' implicitly. Template reference in article suggests asset-exposure hunt is expected standard.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances across infrastructure. Cross-check against patch level for versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Prioritize instances accessible from external networks or without WAF/network segmentation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Unauthenticated Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—truncation is distinct attack surface from creation; second-order impact detection missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file truncation (zero-length writes or rapid shrinking) of configuration files, security tool binaries, or audit logs. Correlate truncation events with Splunk service execution or network requests to PostgreSQL endpoints.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Log/Audit Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file truncation capability could target audit/syslog files; defense-evasion angle not surfaced despite high-risk impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion, truncation, or corruption of audit/syslog files, particularly when preceded by unauthenticated service access or network activity. Detect gaps in continuous logging that align with potential exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Authentication Bypass Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'—authentication bypass detection pattern should be primary hunt vector, absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to Splunk critical endpoints (API, file operations, service administration) that should require authentication but succeed without valid credentials. Flag requests with missing or invalid Authorization/Bearer headers, session tokens, or API keys.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user' to interact with the PostgreSQL sidecar. T1190 exploitation implies accessing a protected service endpoint without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically internal service port or localhost:5432-adjacent) from session contexts with no prior authentication event. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scanner hits. Expected FPs: health checks, monitoring agents with embedded credentials (validate against change control).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability permits 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File-system telemetry should detect unexpected write/delete operations initiated by PostgreSQL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL process for FileCreate/Delete operations outside normal data-directory paths and maintenance windows. Correlate timing with HTTP sidecar endpoint requests. Expected FPs: legitimate database maintenance, vacuum operations (baseline Splunk admin actions).

suggestion.title: POST/PUT to Internal Sidecar File-Operation Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sidecar service endpoint' as attack surface. Detect HTTP methods typically used for write operations (POST, PUT) targeting internal service infrastructure from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify POST or PUT requests to Splunk internal sidecar endpoints with payloads referencing file paths, truncate operations, or SQL file-manipulation verbs. Alert on requests from non-admin users or unexpected source IPs. Expected FPs: legitimate cluster replication traffic (whitelist internal cluster IP ranges).

suggestion.title: Splunk Internal Audit Log Anomalies from Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary files' being created/truncated. Splunk audit.log should capture anomalous internal file operations initiated by low-privilege or unauthorized contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk audit.log for FileCreate/FileDelete events from PostgreSQL sidecar process or unauthenticated user tokens. Alert on operations targeting non-data directories (e.g., config, etc/ paths). Expected FPs: scheduled jobs with sidecar credentials, known maintenance scripts (maintain whitelist).

suggestion.title: Symlink-based TAR traversal in archive extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector as 'TAR traversal with symlinks' to escape the intended directory and read `/etc/shadow`, `~/.ssh/`, AWS credentials. Current UC_103_3 detects file access but not the traversal mechanism itself. Need to detect symlink creation preceding sensitive file reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symbolic link creation events (ln -s, symlink syscalls) within temporary directories (e.g., /tmp, /var/tmp) coinciding with archive extraction activities by Langflow processes, followed by file-read events targeting sensitive paths outside the extract directory.

suggestion.title: Archive extraction followed by recursive sensitive-file discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workflow: file upload → archive extraction → TAR traversal. No detection currently maps archive extraction. Should detect extraction tools (tar, unzip, 7z) spawned by or within Langflow processes followed immediately by find/locate commands targeting credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archive extraction processes (tar, unzip, 7z, bsdtar) spawned by python/uvicorn/gunicorn with Langflow context, followed within 5 seconds by find, locate, grep, or ls commands querying credential-file paths (id_rsa, shadow, passwd, .aws, .ssh).

suggestion.title: Credential file exfiltration after Langflow RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via Python interpreter, but no detection addresses post-exploitation exfiltration of stolen credentials. After arbitrary file read succeeds, attacker must exfiltrate (cat to stdout, curl POST, base64 encode for output channel).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-file read (UC_103_3) with outbound network connections (HTTPS POST, DNS TXT queries, or stdout piping) from the same Langflow process, particularly base64-encoded payloads or repeated outbound connections to non-standard ports within 60 seconds of credential access.

suggestion.title: Python eval/exec gadget invocation in Langflow workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'Python Interpreter RCE' but doesn't explain *how* Python code is injected/executed (eval, exec, pickle.loads, importlib, etc.). Specific gadget detection could tighten detection: look for dangerous Python functions in Langflow worker logs or child process commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow Python worker for invocation of dangerous functions in source code or child process arguments: eval(), exec(), __import__(), pickle.loads(), compile(), ast.literal_eval() with untrusted input, or importlib.import_module() in contexts where input derives from uploaded files or user API parameters.

suggestion.title: Langflow configuration file / secret_key enumeration and extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article lists `secret_key` and `private_key.pem` as targets in UC_103_3 hunt, implying Langflow stores secrets in readable files. Should detect explicit enumeration or direct read of Langflow-specific config paths (e.g., ~/.langflow/config.json, /opt/langflow/secret_key).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to Langflow-specific configuration and credential files (e.g., paths containing 'langflow', 'secret_key', 'config.json', '.langflow/') by processes not owned by the Langflow service account, or by Langflow processes operating under suspicious parent or with suspicious command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation Langflow log tampering or deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly mention log deletion, but post-exploitation attackers typically sanitize logs. Should detect deletion or truncation of Langflow worker logs or application logs coinciding with RCE/credential access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deletion, truncation, or modification of Langflow application logs (e.g., /var/log/langflow*, /opt/langflow/logs/*) by Python/uvicorn/gunicorn processes or their children, especially within 10 minutes after successful shell spawning (UC_103_4) or credential access (UC_103_3).

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation via Supply-Chain PoC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Once the victim clones a malicious repository, a trojanized package named frint is automatically fetched and installed.' This is T1195.002 supply-chain abuse but zero use cases captured the package installation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python package manager (pip) for installation of packages from PyPI that are pulled as dependencies of cloned repositories from GitHub, particularly when repository names match PoC exploit patterns. Flag installations of `frint`, `skytext`, `slogsec`, `logcrypt.cryptography` or similar obfuscated package names.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Native Python Extension Loading and Decryption
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'skytext, which contains a compiled native Python extension. When the PoC executes, the extension runs automatically and decrypts additional embedded Python code.' This decryption of embedded payloads is a distinct defense-evasion step not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter spawning child processes or loading .so/.pyd files immediately after importing packages from pip, followed by in-process code decryption or execution of previously-obfuscated bytecode. Monitor for Python processes loading native extensions from unusual temp directories.

suggestion.title: Mapbox Dataset Abuse for C2 Communication and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals: 'ChocoPoC...from a Mapbox dataset' and 'Mapbox datasets are also abused for data exfiltration.' This is infrastructure-level C2 abuse requiring HTTP/API monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to `mapbox.com` or Mapbox API endpoints originating from Python processes, especially those spawned from unusual source repositories. Monitor for data exfiltration patterns in Mapbox requests (encoded credential, file, or process data).

suggestion.title: Bulk Browser Credential and Cookies Extraction by Research Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChocoPoC capability: 'collect browser passwords, cookies, autofill data, and browsing history.' This is credential access (T1555) that should trigger detection when executed from PoC/research tool context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python or shell processes accessing browser credential stores (e.g., `~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Login Data`, `~/Library/Keychains`, Edge/Firefox profile directories) when spawned from cloned git repositories or package installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Sensitive Files by Type (Markdown, Database, Archives)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'search for text files, markdown documentation files, and database files.' This targeted file discovery is distinct collection behavior not typical of benign PoC execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python/shell processes launched from git clone directories performing recursive filesystem enumerations filtering on file extensions (.md, .txt, .db, .sqlite, .json, .yaml, .conf). Flag processes accessing multiple sensitive file types in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Shell History and Network Configuration Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists ChocoPoC capabilities: 'gather shell history from the host collect network configuration.' These are post-exploitation discovery actions typical of RAT lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading shell history files (~/.bash_history, ~/.zsh_history, ~/.sh_history) and network configuration files (/etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/network/interfaces, ipconfig output) when spawned from non-shell/admin contexts or from Python interpreters.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Unpatched Argo CD Repo-Server Flaw Could Let Attackers Take Over Kubernetes Clusters'—core attack is repo-server vulnerability exploitation. Pipeline missed detection of exploitation attempts or anomalous process execution within repo-server container.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Argo CD repo-server process for unexpected child processes, shell spawning, or system utility execution (curl, wget, bash) outside normal git/helm fetch workflows. Alert on repo-server attempting outbound connections to attacker infrastructure or accessing /proc filesystem.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Repository Credential Access from Argo CD
suggestion.rationale: Argo CD fetches manifests from Git repositories using stored credentials. Unpatched server compromised = credential exfiltration likely. Pipeline missed detection of service account secret enumeration or Git credential abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track reads of Argo CD service account secrets containing Git credentials. Alert on secret access patterns anomalies, failed git clone attempts followed by successful ones with different IP source, or Git operations from non-standard Argo CD pod IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Application Deployment via Compromised Argo CD
suggestion.rationale: Attack premise is cluster takeover via Argo CD—attacker injects malicious manifests through compromised repo-server. Pipeline missed detection of unexpected ApplicationSet/Application creation or manifest drift with privilege escalation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for new Argo CD Applications/ApplicationSets with suspicious spec elements: privileged=true, hostNetwork, hostPID, mountPath to /var/run/docker.sock, or service account tokens. Alert on manifest syncs deploying unsigned/untrusted container images.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Service Account RBAC Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Cluster 'takeover' requires elevated permissions post-compromise. Article implies attacker gains cluster control—pipeline missed detection of service account token exfiltration or sudden RBAC binding changes granting cluster-admin rights.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding creation referencing Argo CD service accounts with cluster-admin or wildcarded verb permissions. Alert on sudden elevation of Argo CD service account privileges, especially if paired with new ApplicationSet deployments.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Backdoored Argo CD Application
suggestion.rationale: Takeover implies sustained access—attacker deploys persistent backdoor workloads through Argo CD. Pipeline missed detection of long-lived attacker-controlled pods or configuration-as-code persistence patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Argo CD Application/ApplicationSet resources pointing to attacker-controlled Git repositories or registry servers. Alert on pods with unusual image pull policies, external image registries, or DaemonSet/StatefulSet deployments with high restart counts or init containers executing network tools.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Kubernetes Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Cluster 'takeover' enables lateral movement to other infrastructure. Article scope implies attacker gains broad cluster access and potentially cloud/network access—pipeline missed detection of cloud credential exfiltration or multi-cluster spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor deployed pods for kubectl execution, cloud metadata service access (AWS IMDS 169.254.169.254, Azure metadata endpoint), or attempts to read kubeconfig/cloud credentials from /root/.kube or /.aws. Alert on containers spawning bash/sh with outbound connections to non-cluster IPs or launching reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MFA Bypass or MFA Reset Activity
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider is known for social engineering to gain access and bypass MFA. Article title references hacking charges implying unauthorized access; Scattered Spider's signature move is defeating 2FA/MFA through social engineering or credential stuffing. No use case covered initial access defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unusual MFA challenge patterns, MFA method changes by non-owner accounts, repeated MFA denials followed by successful login, or MFA resets initiated outside business hours or unusual locations. Flag bulk MFA resets on service accounts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing and Brute Force Against Enterprise Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider uses large-scale credential brute forcing. Title mentions 'hacking charges' and group is known for password spray attacks. Pipeline missed detection for high-volume failed login attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >10 failed login attempts from single source IP per user in 5 min window; >50 unique users targeted from single IP in 1 hour; failed logins followed by success from same source within 60 min; distributed attack patterns across time zones.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Valid Compromised Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Once Scattered Spider gains credentials, they move laterally. Article describes an extradited suspect (implying substantive investigation finding lateral movement). No use case for detecting lateral movement post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised-credential usage: same account logging in from multiple unusual IPs in short span; service account interactive logins; RDP/SSH activity from non-standard source networks; lateral movement to administrative/sensitive systems via valid credentials.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Information Gathering Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider performs extensive OSINT and directory enumeration. Pipeline missed detection for pre-attack reconnaissance. Article title does not describe this phase but is implicit in extradition investigation scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for bulk user/group enumeration queries, excessive Get-ADUser/Get-ADGroup PowerShell commands, API calls to user directory endpoints, or probing of sensitive resource shares followed by compromise attempts hours/days later.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Financial or Customer Data
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider's motivation is financial fraud/extortion. Extradition suggests data theft occurred. Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting data staging, compression, or exfil of bulk customer/financial records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file copies to temp directories, zip/7z/rar compression of customer databases, large uploads to cloud storage (Box/Dropbox/Mega), file access to sensitive finance/customer DBs followed by external network connections to hosting/proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package Installation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'tells you which machine pulled a compromised package'—core detection gap is identifying machines that fetched or installed a known-malicious package version from a registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager processes (npm, pip, nuget, maven) for installation/fetch operations targeting known-compromised package names or versions. Correlate machine identity with package download timestamps to identify affected endpoints. Flag any machine pulling a package flagged in threat intelligence as malicious or signed by untrusted source.

suggestion.title: Registry Authentication Anomalies on Package Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a feature that tracks 'which machine' pulled packages—implies authentication/authorization logging at registry layer; missing detection for unexpected machine identities or geographic anomalies pulling sensitive packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry API access logs (package.json resolution, artifact metadata queries) for authentication from unexpected machine identifiers, IPs, or credential pairs. Detect lateral movement via package pulling from machines not typically assigned package management duties.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Manager Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses detection of package pulls; supply chain attacks pivot through package install commands—need detection for unexpected or obfuscated package manager invocations on endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious package manager command lines: --skip-verify, --insecure, inline credential injection, redirecting stderr, unsigned/untrusted repository URL overrides, or execution from non-standard paths. Correlate with elevated privileges or scheduled task execution.

suggestion.title: Machine-to-Compromised-Package Correlation Index
suggestion.rationale: Core theme of article ('tells you which machine') implies forensic correlation capability; detection gap is proactive scanning of endpoint package manifests (package-lock.json, requirements.txt, .csproj) against threat-intel package blacklist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect and parse package dependency files from all endpoints. Compare declared/pinned versions against curated list of known-malicious package versions from CVE/threat feeds. Alert on any endpoint with a compromised package in active dependency tree.

suggestion.title: Registry Repository Metadata Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package implies upstream repository compromise; detection gap for identifying when package metadata (checksums, signatures, timestamps) diverge from expected baseline or show signs of replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate package signatures and checksums at download time; flag mismatches against published registry metadata. Detect MITM or replay attacks by comparing download content hash against current registry manifest. Alert on certificate pinning violations or unexpected certificate chains during registry queries.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Must detect initial access attempts lacking auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT to Splunk sidecar endpoints (port 5432 or service APIs) missing Authorization headers or returning 401 before file operations. Baseline normal Splunk service-to-service traffic; flag external or unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary file creation/truncation via Splunk sidecar exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack payload: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Detection focuses on impact phase—successful exploitation writes/deletes files on target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or deletion in Splunk config directories (app.conf, limits.conf, default.conf) or sidecar temp paths correlated with preceding unauthenticated API requests. Flag truncation of critical files as high-confidence exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Standard inventory-based detection referenced in source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner output and asset inventory for CVE-2026-20253 findings on Splunk Enterprise installations. Escalate any unpatched finding after federal due date 2026-06-21. Cross-reference against network exposure (public-facing vs. internal).

suggestion.title: Splunk version enumeration and reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must identify Splunk versions to target vulnerable deployments. Article implies public-facing endpoint; reconnaissance precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Splunk banner endpoints (/en-US/account/login, /services/system/info, /_internal/*) or User-Agent strings from scanners (Shodan, Censys, Metasploit). Successful responses leak version strings (e.g., 'Splunk Enterprise 9.1.0').

suggestion.title: Public-facing Splunk inventory and network exposure audit
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'canonical asset-exposure hunt' for CISA KEV; active exploitation targets internet-reachable Splunk instances. Core preventative detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall rules and load-balancer configs for Splunk web/API ports (8000, 8089, 443/8089, 5432) reachable from untrusted networks. Enumerate all internet-facing Splunk instances; cross-check patch status against CVE-2026-20253. Flag any public-facing unpatched instance as critical.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL sidecar service traffic patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface. Attacker must communicate with service; anomalous query patterns or source IPs indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal sidecar traffic (expected Splunk internal sources, query patterns). Flag inbound traffic from external sources, non-Splunk processes, or unusual PostgreSQL queries (CREATE TABLE, DROP, SELECT information_schema) originating from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack surface: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline produced zero detection for this exposed internal service being accessed without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk sidecar port (typically 8000-9000 range) for unauthenticated session initiation. Alert on repeated failed→successful connection pairs (scanning signature), source IPs outside trusted Splunk infrastructure networks, or unusual TLS handshake failures followed by successful negotiation. Baseline normal internal traffic and flag geographic or external-origin anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation and Truncation via Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar.' Pipeline generated zero file-system impact detection despite file tampering being the direct exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events in Splunk installation directories (e.g., /opt/splunk, %SPLUNK_HOME%) executed by splunkd service account without corresponding deployment/configuration push events. Flag rapid file-operation bursts, writes to config files or system directories, and truncation of log files. Correlate with sidecar service restarts or inbound network traffic to sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Scanner Findings Correlated with Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' using vulnerability scanner; pipeline produced no detection pairing scan results (exploitable version) with network evidence (listening sidecar port, inbound traffic). Patch lag post federal due-date (2026-06-21) is high-confidence exploitation risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each CVE-2026-20253 scanner positive: verify Splunk Enterprise version in asset database, cross-reference with Splunk advisory for vulnerable versions. Correlate with network logs showing sidecar port (8000-8999) in LISTEN state and inbound traffic from non-Splunk sources. Escalate if scanner date > 2026-06-21 (federal remediation deadline), indicating patch lag.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempts to Sidecar Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'missing authentication for critical function'—the vulnerability is the absence of auth enforcement. Pipeline should have detected early-stage exploitation reconnaissance patterns (unauthenticated request attempts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Splunk audit logs, hunt for unauthenticated connection attempts to sidecar endpoints (HTTP 401 responses, missing or invalid Bearer tokens in _internal logs). Alert on repeated POST/PUT requests to sidecar API without valid session credentials. Check for exploitation patterns: slow attempts followed by rapid success (scanner → exploit transition). Monitor for requests carrying file-operation payloads (e.g., 'truncate', 'create') without authentication.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Splunk Service Process Behavior Indicating Post-Exploitation File Ops
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, the sidecar service will execute file operations triggered by attacker requests. Pipeline missed behavioral detection for suspicious splunkd process activity correlating with network access to sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor splunkd process for abnormal file operations (writes to sensitive dirs like /etc, /var, or application binaries). Alert on child processes spawned by splunkd without corresponding config deployment events. Correlate file-write events with inbound network traffic to sidecar port—if file ops occur within seconds of external connection, flag as potential exploitation.

suggestion.title: Baseline Splunk Sidecar Network Traffic and Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Sidecar is internal microservice; legitimate traffic should be from Splunk components only. Pipeline generated no baseline or anomaly detection for this network surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of sidecar traffic: source IPs (should be localhost, other Splunk containers/services), destination port (sidecar port), protocol (HTTP/gRPC), data volume, and frequency. Alert on new external sources, geographic anomalies (traffic from countries outside org), sustained connection attempts, or data exfiltration patterns (large outbound traffic post-file-creation). Flag if sidecar becomes accessible from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the exploitation mechanism and primary detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated or failed-auth connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar ports on Splunk infrastructure. Correlate successful connections from external IP ranges with subsequent file creation/deletion in Splunk data directories.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise External Exposure Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires unauthenticated access; vulnerability is only viable if Splunk instances or sidecar endpoints are externally facing. Article provides no ACL/firewall context, implying exposure is a prerequisite threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run asset scan for Splunk Enterprise instances accessible from untrusted networks (WAN, internet). Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-20253. Flag any unpatched external-facing instances; prioritize remediation by federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the attack outcome. This is the post-exploitation impact and primary forensic indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation, truncation, or deletion events on Splunk infrastructure initiated by sidecar/PostgreSQL processes outside normal installation paths. Alert on system-critical or configuration file modifications (e.g., /etc/*, Splunk/etc/apps).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match and Patch Gap Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article template explicitly instructs to 'match against your vulnerability scanner' with this CVE; CISA KEV entries require active scanning correlation. Pipeline did not capture CVE as an IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run weekly scans for CVE-2026-20253 across all Splunk Enterprise systems. Correlate 'vulnerable' results with patch inventory. Flag patch lag > 3 days post-federal deadline (2026-06-21) for escalation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unexpected Process or Shell Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires the sidecar to accept and act on unauthenticated commands. Unusual process spawning (shell, file utilities) from sidecar context indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bash, sh, powershell, or file utility (touch, rm, dd) process creation by PostgreSQL or Splunk sidecar processes. Alert on any shell invocation; baseline legitimate sidecar operations first.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Port Listening on World-Routable Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is only exploitable if sidecar endpoint accepts unauthenticated requests from network; exposure on 0.0.0.0 or public-facing IPs is the prerequisite threat condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify Splunk sidecar (typically port 5432 or vendor-documented port) does NOT bind to 0.0.0.0 or external IP interfaces. Alert if sidecar process is configured to listen on untrusted network segments or if firewall rules permit inbound unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct exploitation surface requiring endpoint authentication audit
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (/postgresql, /sidecar) that lack authentication headers, produce 200-series responses, or show successful connection without LOGIN events. Correlate with subsequent file I/O in PostgreSQL transaction logs.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow...to create or truncate arbitrary files' — impact surface requiring query audit and filesystem monitoring
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on COPY/CREATE/TRUNCATE/UNLINK operations in PostgreSQL audit logs issued without a preceding authentication event or issued by null/default user contexts. Exclude maintenance windows and scheduled backups.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Splunk Enterprise with CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253 unpatched status. Cross-reference with network asset topology to identify instances reachable from untrusted zones; these are immediate exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Service Port Accessibility from External Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface; requires network perimeter assessment of service exposure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify all Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar services (default port 5432) are NOT routable from DMZ or internet-facing zones. Audit firewall egress rules for unexpected outbound PostgreSQL connections from Splunk hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect File Deletion/Truncation Anomalies Targeting Splunk Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'truncate arbitrary files' — attackers may destroy data, logs, or configs; requires behavioral anomaly detection on target filesystem
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file deletion or truncation operations within $SPLUNK_HOME (config, etc, var directories) that originate from localhost (PostgreSQL process) outside change-management windows. Combine with connection logs to isolate to sidecar requests.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the core exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (/services/sidecar/*, /api/sidecar/*, /pg/*) that lack valid authentication headers (missing Authorization, session cookie, or auth token) originating from external IPs. Successful exploitation will trigger POST/PUT/DELETE operations on filesystem resources.

suggestion.title: Detect Newly Exposed Splunk Enterprise Instances
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploits 'public-facing application' vulnerability; CISA KEV requires active exploitation against exposed assets. Standard asset-exposure hunt for ports 8000 (web), 8089 (mgmt).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Splunk instances across internal network. Cross-reference against external IP space (Shodan, port scan logs, WAF public IP logs). Flag any Splunk instances (port 8000, 8089) newly visible from untrusted IP ranges (non-RFC1918, non-corporate ranges).

suggestion.title: Detect PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must discover the vulnerable endpoint before exploitation. Article mentions specific endpoint type but doesn't name it—reconnaissance step precedes the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for repeated HTTP requests (404, 403, 401 responses) to sidecar-related paths from single source IP in short time window (5-10 min). Patterns: /services/sidecar*, /api/v1/sidecar*, /postgres*, /pg/*. Spike in 404s against Splunk instances may indicate vulnerability scanning.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar API
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—successful exploitation has distinct file-system or DB-operation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 200/201 responses to sidecar endpoints with subsequent filesystem DELETE, TRUNCATE, or CREATE operations. In Splunk logs, look for API responses containing 'success' or status 200 immediately followed by file modification events. Filesize drop to zero on critical files (config, database) post-sidecar API call is strong indicator.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'CVE-2026-20253—match against your vulnerability scanner.' Direct IOC pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signature for known exploitation payloads: requests containing parameter names like 'query', 'cmd', 'execute' sent to /services/sidecar or /api endpoints; or User-Agent patterns known to exploit this CVE. IDS/WAF rules should key on lack of auth context + sidecar endpoint access + any of: CREATE, TRUNCATE, DELETE in request body.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Port Exposure to Internet
suggestion.rationale: Standard asset-exposure hunt for public-facing application. Article references template for asset-exposure which baseline-hunts for externally reachable Splunk ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference firewall rules and WAF logs for inbound traffic to ports 8000 (Splunk web), 8089 (mgmt), 8191 (KV store) from non-internal IP ranges. Verify ACLs actually block untrusted CIDR blocks. High FP rate in cloud/hybrid environments—baseline against org's intentional public Splunk instances (if any).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure from External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploitable via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' by unauthenticated users. This is the initial access vector and should trigger on unexpected external connections to the sidecar port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to PostgreSQL default port (5432) or Splunk sidecar ports from external/unauthenticated sources against Splunk Enterprise instances. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to the sidecar service. High fidelity if source IPs are non-corporate and no patch indicators are present in vulnerability management.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the impact phase and should detect abnormal file operations originating from PostgreSQL processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or deletion events originating from PostgreSQL sidecar service processes where the originating user context is unauthenticated or the process runs with unexpected privilege escalation. Flag any writes to system-critical directories or config files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article directs to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template in referenced TEMPLATES.md. Pipeline should instantiate template-based detection for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances and version them against CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scope. Combine with network exposure scans to flag externally-reachable instances. Federal patch deadline is 2026-06-21; non-compliance should escalate.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Go Module Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt'—attackers relied on name similarity to fool developers into installing the backdoored version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Go module imports where package name exhibits high string similarity (Damerau-Levenshtein distance <3) to known legitimate packages. Alert on installations of packages with suspiciously altered names (e.g., botdb-go/bolt vs boltdb/bolt). Correlate with Go vulnerability database entries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Module Version Update to Known Malicious Release
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years'—detection should flag updates to v1.3.1 of botdb-go/bolt and similar known-malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency update operations for suspicious version pinning or update to specific known-malicious Go module versions (e.g., github.com/botdb-go/bolt@v1.3.1). Cross-reference against Go vulnerability database (GO-2025-3451) and Snyk advisory SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841.

suggestion.title: Go Module Proxy Cache Anomaly—Package Served After Source Removal
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' and 'The Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients' even after GitHub removal—this is an infrastructure-level persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect packages accessible via Go Module Proxy (proxy.golang.org) that no longer exist in canonical source repositories (GitHub). Establish baseline of legitimate cached packages and flag packages with removal timestamps that predate recent download activity.

suggestion.title: C&C Communication from Infected Go Application
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server'—this indicates network-based C&C beaconing that should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from Go processes (those importing github.com/botdb-go/bolt). Flag connections to known or suspicious C&C infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries from Go applications for domains not in baseline. Correlate process execution (go run, go build output) with suspicious network patterns.

suggestion.title: Go Dependency Manifest Tampering or Unexpected Module Appearance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 3-year undetected persistence: attackers exploited Go's caching model to keep malicious code active. Detection should identify anomalous module manifests or unexpected dependency introduction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan go.mod and go.sum files for unexpected or suspicious module entries. Alert when go.sum hash for a module differs between cached and live versions. Monitor for undocumented dependency introductions or version pinning to unusual/old versions.

suggestion.title: Package Registry Typo-Squatting Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates systematic typo squatting: 'bad actors create and upload harmful software packages to online libraries using names very similar to popular ones.'  Preventive detection should identify malicious packages before widespread adoption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Apply edit-distance algorithms to newly published Go packages; flag packages with names ≤2–3 character edits from established packages (especially those >1yr old with significant adoption). Flag packages with zero commit history or recently-created accounts uploading similarly-named packages. Cross-reference against known legitimate package ownership.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct attack path and requires detection of lateral/internal access to the sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/network requests to internal PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or custom) without authentication headers. Alert on successful connections from external or undesired internal segments. Correlate with Splunk instance exposure scanning.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection must capture file-system writes initiated by the sidecar process or API calls that delegate to it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file creation/modification events by Splunk sidecar process (or parent Splunk daemon) writing to unexpected paths (outside Splunk home, config dirs, or known temp locations). Correlate with preceding unauthenticated endpoint access. Truncation (zero-length writes) is especially suspicious.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match + Patch Lag Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Standard asset-exposure template hunt referenced but not operationalized.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference scanner detections for CVE-2026-20253 against patch-deployment records. Identify Splunk Enterprise instances with patch-date prior to 2026-06-21 and confirmed vulnerable config (sidecar enabled, exposed). Prioritize by CVSS (critical per article header) and internet-facing status.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposure on Public Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article references: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt—the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].' Template substitution required with CVE-2026-20253; pipeline failed to instantiate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network perimeter logs for inbound traffic to known Splunk ports (8000/web, 8089/mgmt, custom sidecar endpoints). Cross-reference source IPs against public IP registries. Alert on connections from ASNs outside trust list. Combine with vulnerability scanner to identify exposed unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Startup or Configuration Change
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is the sidecar endpoint. Article does not detail default ports or configs, but threat actors must either access an exposed sidecar or be positioned internally. Detection should cover service enablement or configuration drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Splunk sidecar service (PostgreSQL or wrapper process) starting with unusual arguments or user context. Flag config changes enabling network exposure (e.g., listen on 0.0.0.0) or removing authentication. Correlate timing with CVE-2026-20253 disclosure date (2026-06-18).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Primary attack vector; zero detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service (typically port 8191 or configured endpoint) for requests without valid authentication tokens/session cookies. Flag any unauthenticated HTTP 200 response (successful request). Correlate source IPs with public ASNs; internal-only traffic is lower risk than external exploitation.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' is the measurable impact. No post-exploitation detection generated despite this being the exploitation payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Splunk daemon and PostgreSQL sidecar processes (splunkd, postgres) writing to directories outside SPLUNK_HOME. Alert on file truncation (size → 0) or deletion of system-critical paths (/etc/passwd, config files). Monitor file descriptors opened in write mode from sidecar child processes spawning shells.

suggestion.title: Internet-Accessible Splunk Instances Vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article implies 'exposed assets' and 'public-facing application' but pipeline generated no asset-inventory or network-exposure detection despite CISA KEV demanding urgent scope validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/inventory for Splunk instances (port 8000, 8088, 8191) reachable from internet-routed sources without VPN gating. Cross-reference with patch-status database for pre-patched versions. Correlate with external scanning datasets (Censys, Shodan) showing exposed Splunk UI. Prioritize for emergency patching if internet-routable post-2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance + Scanner Detection Match
suggestion.rationale: Article provides CVE ID and federal due-date (2026-06-21) but pipeline extracted zero vulnerability IOCs. Baseline scanner correlation is mandatory for CISA KEV operationalization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Splunk Enterprise instances in scanner output showing CVE-2026-20253 match. Cross-reference patch-management system for deployment status. Generate weekly compliance report of un-patched instances post-due-date. Verify patches via Splunk _internal index logs showing version bump in startup messages.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Process Behavioral Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article names PostgreSQL sidecar as exploitation channel but pipeline generated zero process-level detections. Baseline and continuous monitoring of this service is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for PostgreSQL sidecar: parent process (splunkd), user context (splunk), network listeners (server-only, no outbound). Alert on deviations: sidecar spawning shell (bash, sh, powershell), new file descriptors to non-Splunk directories, unexpected network state (client connections initiated from sidecar), or elevated privileges. Monitor for sidecar process being signaled/controlled by unexpected parents.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Signals Against Splunk Critical API Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'—root cause. Article explicitly names auth failure as enabler but pipeline generated no bypass-detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit.log for unauthenticated successful API calls to /services/ or /api/ endpoints (HTTP 200 without Authorization header or valid session). Baseline should show 0% unauthenticated success; any deviation = investigate. Look for HTTP 401 → retry → HTTP 200 pattern suggesting bypass attempt. Correlate with source IPs making rapid sequential requests to enumerate endpoints.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack vector and must be hunted as the primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints. Baseline legitimate service communication and alert on requests with no credentials or failed auth headers. Look for endpoints typically on non-standard ports (5432 sidecar proxy variants) on Splunk hosts.

suggestion.title: Splunk File Truncation via PostgreSQL Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the exploitation objective and must be detected. File operations initiated via unauthenticated service endpoints are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/truncation on Splunk Enterprise hosts that originates from PostgreSQL sidecar service context or from unauthenticated callers. Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk file operations and alert on anomalies, especially truncation of config, auth, or logging files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposed Service Endpoint Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires discovery of the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint; article notes this is 'public-facing' (T1190 implies exposure). Detection should identify reconnaissance for these non-standard service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for scanning/enumeration activity targeting Splunk Enterprise hosts on non-standard service ports, especially PostgreSQL sidecar ports. Look for repeated connection attempts, failed auth probes, or port scans originating from external sources against exposed Splunk infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication Bypass on Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: CVE explicitly describes 'missing authentication for critical function.' Detections should surface attempts to invoke critical Splunk functions without credentials, which indicates exploitation or active probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk authentication/authorization logs for unauthenticated or improperly-authenticated calls to critical functions (file operations, configuration changes, user management). Flag requests that bypass normal auth flow or originate from service accounts with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Pattern — Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies this CVE is in active exploitation (CISA KEV status). Detection should look for known exploitation signatures or behavioral patterns unique to this vulnerability's attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise that match known CVE-2026-20253 exploitation patterns: POST requests to sidecar endpoints with file-operation payloads, or requests containing PostgreSQL command injection strings. Cross-reference against public POC/exploit indicators.

suggestion.title: Splunk Config or Auth File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gaining unauthenticated file manipulation will likely target Splunk config, user auth files, or license files. Truncation of these files disables features or deletes audit trails. File integrity monitoring is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any unauthorized modification, truncation, or deletion of Splunk critical files (auth.conf, limits.conf, inputs.conf, user-seed.conf) or Splunk internal directories. Use file integrity monitoring with strict baseline; flag both direct filesystem changes and any sidecar-service-initiated changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is direct exploitation of T1190 without any authentication requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Splunk instances for requests targeting PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (commonly /services/admin/sidecar or direct port 5432 access patterns) originating from external/untrusted networks. Flag requests that lack valid Splunk session cookies or authentication headers. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scanner hits.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Splunk Sidecar (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—the impact phase of successful exploitation, requiring file-system and application log monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise audit and PostgreSQL sidecar logs for file creation, deletion, or truncation events initiated without authenticated user context. Track modifications to $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/, conf files, and system directories. Establish baseline of legitimate file ops; alert on anomalies, especially targeting configuration or credential storage paths.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Enterprise Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status means active wild exploitation of exposed instances. Article targets 'public-facing' Splunk vulnerable to unauthenticated access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253.
