suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation (frint/skytext/slogsec)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names trojanized packages on PyPI: 'Once the victim clones a malicious repository, a trojanized package named frint is automatically fetched and installed.' These are actionable, time-sensitive IOCs that warrant immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/python package managers for installation of known-malicious packages (frint, skytext, slogsec, logcrypt.cryptography). Inspect setup.py or requirements.txt in cloned repositories for suspicious dependency chains. Alert on first-time package installations from PyPI with zero historical prevalence or linked to security researcher activity.

suggestion.title: Native Python Extension Loading from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the package pulls a malicious dependency package, skytext, which contains a compiled native Python extension. When the PoC executes, the extension runs automatically.' This is a key evasion tactic hiding malicious code in .so/.pyd files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter loading compiled extensions (.so, .pyd) from temporary directories, package cache (site-packages), or non-standard paths. Cross-reference loaded extension names against PyPI package manifests. Alert on extensions with no public symbol table or loaded immediately post-pip-install.

suggestion.title: Decryption/Code Invocation by Python Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes obfuscated payload delivery: 'extension runs automatically and decrypts additional embedded Python code that triggers a downloader.' This defense-evasion step should trigger behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes for crypto library imports (hashlib, cryptography, Crypto) followed by decrypt-like operations on embedded data. Detect loading of base64/hex-encoded payloads followed by exec() or importlib calls. Alert on Python child processes spawned within milliseconds of extension load.

suggestion.title: Mapbox Dataset Access for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies C2 channel: 'ChocoPoC, from a Mapbox dataset' and 'Mapbox datasets are also abused for data exfiltration.' Direct IOC for C2 beaconing and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to api.mapbox.com or datasets.mapbox.com from Python processes, especially those spawned by package managers or PoC scripts. Alert on requests with unusual dataset IDs or access patterns. Correlate with browser-data-theft indicators (stolen cookies, passwords in outbound traffic).

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Extraction by Python Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RAT capability: 'collect browser passwords, cookies, autofill data, and browsing history.' Detect Python accessing browser storage directories and Chrome/Firefox credential databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python processes opening browser credential files (Chrome/profile*/Login Data, Firefox profile sqlite databases, Edge Local State). Detect imports of sqlite3 or keyring libraries by scripts spawned via package installation. Monitor for tar/zip operations on ~/.config/chromium or ~/.mozilla directories.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Process and Network Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists RAT capabilities: 'enumerate running processes', 'gather shell history from the host', 'collect network configuration.' These discovery activities can be detected in sequence after infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python child processes executing ps, netstat, ifconfig, or uname commands in rapid succession. Monitor for Python libraries querying psutil or subprocess for process lists. Alert on combination: pip install → Python extension load → subprocess calls to system discovery tools → data collection.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states flaw in repo-server component allows cluster takeover. No use case was generated to detect exploitation attempts against this public-facing service endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Argo CD repo-server API endpoints (typically /api/v1/repositories, /metrics, or repo-server pod ports 8081-8084) from external sources with unusual payloads, SQL injection patterns, template injection markers, or request paths not consistent with legitimate GitOps operations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Kubernetes Cluster Admin Role Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'take over Kubernetes clusters'—implying privilege escalation to cluster-admin. No detection for unauthorized RBAC modifications or service account privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of cluster-role-bindings binding non-system service accounts to cluster-admin role, new service accounts with elevated privileges, or unusual kubectl exec/auth commands executed from within Argo CD namespace post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Pod Escape / Host Breakout Detection
suggestion.rationale: Cluster takeover via repo-server likely involves container escape or privilege escalation out of the Argo CD pod. No detection scenario addresses unusual process execution or volume mounts from the compromised pod.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Argo CD repo-server pods for execution of shell interpreters, system binaries (mount, nsenter, chroot), or processes spawning outside expected repo-server application context. Alert on attempts to access host filesystem via /proc or /sys, or binding to privileged ports.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Application/Secret Tampering for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Attackers controlling repo-server can manipulate deployed applications or inject secrets for persistence. No UC covers unauthorized modifications to GitOps config repositories or Argo CD application definitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized commits to Git repositories linked to Argo CD, new Secrets/ConfigMaps created in argocd namespace with suspicious patterns, or application manifests modified to deploy backdoor containers, reverse shells, or additional service accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Argo CD Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting repo-server provides attackers with Argo CD's cluster credentials and kubeconfig. Pipeline missed detection for lateral movement to other namespaces or clusters managed by Argo CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected kubectl API calls to clusters other than the Argo CD cluster using Argo CD service account credentials, access to kubeconfig secrets stored in argocd namespace, or sudden enumeration of secrets across multiple namespaces post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from Argo CD Cluster Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full cluster takeover; pipeline should have flagged detection of exfiltration or C2 communication originating from the compromised cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from Argo CD pods and nodes for connections to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, unusual protocols (DNS tunneling, ICMP, non-standard ports), or patterns consistent with reverse shell or exfiltration traffic.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Phishing and Social Engineering Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names Scattered Spider, a group known for social engineering vectors; pipeline should have mapped initial-access detections for phishing emails, credential-phishing, and impersonation attempts targeting high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with URL shorteners, lookalike domains, or sender spoofing from untrusted external sources. Flag conversation threads building rapport before requesting credentials or sensitive access information.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Credential Enumeration and Targeted Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Group methodology involves testing stolen credentials across multiple systems and cloud services; detection should cover account enumeration and auth anomalies preceding successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid user enumeration (failed user lookups) followed by targeted brute-force or password-spray attempts within short time window. Correlate cloud and on-premises sign-in failures preceding successful authentications.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: SSH Lateral Movement and Interactive Shell Access
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider uses SSH for lateral movement post-compromise; extradition for hacking charges implies investigation uncovered lateral movement activity requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH connections from unusual ASNs or IPs followed by interactive shell spawning (bash, sh, zsh). Alert on shell processes initiated by sshd running as privileged user at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Data Collection and Exfiltration Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses extradition for hacking charges; Scattered Spider stages data via clipboard capture, archive compression, and collection of sensitive files before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing clipboard APIs, browser process memory, or SSH key storage. Detect archive creation (tar, 7z, zip) of ~/.ssh, /home/*/Documents, or cloud-sync directories followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Living-off-the-Land and Shell Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Group avoids deploying malware; uses base64-encoded commands, curl, wget, and shell piping to avoid signatures—detection baseline critical for investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on base64 decoding in command lines, unusual curl/wget with pipe-to-bash patterns, and certutil/bitsadmin used for data transfer. Baseline command patterns per user to detect anomalies.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Persistence via Authorized SSH Keys and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Investigation leading to extradition suggests detection of persistent backdoors; group uses ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and cron jobs for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/config, /root/.ssh/*, or /etc/cron.d/ via file integrity monitoring. Alert on cron jobs containing reverse shells, curl callbacks, or SSH tunneling.

suggestion.title: Package Registry Credential Exposure via Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'tells you which machine pulled a compromised package'—implies detection of machine identity + package pull correlation. No UC captures machine-to-package mapping or registry authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package-manager process execution (npm, pip, maven, nuget) with source machine identity and registry endpoint. Flag pulls to public registries of packages not in baseline deployment manifest. Compare machine identity claimed in registry pull logs to AD/MDM enrollment records to detect lateral movement or workstation impersonation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Execution Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title implies package installation was detected retroactively ('now tells you')—but no detection for post-installation execution of code from compromised package. Should map to T1203 or T1187.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from package installation directories or by package-manager wrapper processes. Alert on unsigned executables or scripts launched from vendor-standard package cache paths (/node_modules, site-packages, lib/, etc.). Correlate process lineage to timestamp of package pull from IOC'd registry.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Hash Mismatch in Registry
suggestion.rationale: A 'Secure Registry' feature detecting compromised packages implies cryptographic validation. No UC for hash or signature mismatch detection between published and installed artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare file hashes of installed packages against published hashes in official registries (or signed manifests). Alert when registry manifest hash differs from local file hash, or when installation bypassed integrity checks (--no-audit, --unsafe-perm flags). Correlate mismatches to machine identity for blast-radius assessment.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TCP connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or mapped) lacking prior authentication. Baseline legitimate Splunk internal traffic. Alert on connections from unexpected source IPs, user contexts, or external networks. Correlate with CVE-2026-20253 asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — direct execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file write or truncate events sourced from postgres.exe or postgres daemon on Splunk hosts, especially in non-standard paths outside /var/lib/splunk or %SPLUNK_HOME%. Flag child processes spawned by PostgreSQL service with file-system write semantics or shell invocation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with observed exploitation and federal patch-due date 2026-06-21. Standard asset-exposure hunt for all KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances; flag vulnerable versions per CVE-2026-20253 advisories. Prioritize instances exposed to untrusted networks. Correlate with patch status and compare against federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Query Execution in Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article implies queries or file-system commands executed via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires audit-log hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar audit logs for unauthenticated or unexpected queries. Flag CREATE, COPY, TRUNCATE, or filesystem-write commands (e.g., COPY ... TO OUTFILE). Alert on commands targeting files or directories outside Splunk's standard schema.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states attacker 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the attack surface is explicit and should trigger detection rule generation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar paths (e.g., /_api/pgsql, internal endpoint patterns) that lack valid Splunk authentication headers or session tokens. Baseline normal administrative access and alert on new sources or spike in failed auth requests.

suggestion.title: Detect File Creation/Truncation Correlated with Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploit outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file manipulation is the direct impact and should correlate with endpoint access logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP access to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints with subsequent file creation or truncation events on the Splunk host filesystem. Look for unexpected temporary files or truncated log files immediately following unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Inventory and Patch Splunk Enterprise Instances for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV badge indicates active exploitation; article emphasizes 'even if your scanners say not vulnerable because of patches, it's worth one quick check'—asset inventory hunt is critical
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Splunk Enterprise instances for version and patch status against CVE-2026-20253. Cross-check with external network exposure data (Shodan, certificate transparency, passive DNS) to identify internet-facing instances. Prioritize remediation by external reachability and time-to-patch.

suggestion.title: Monitor PostgreSQL Sidecar for Abnormal File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is specific to sidecar service behavior; unusual file I/O (CREATE, TRUNCATE, WRITE) from sidecar process indicates exploitation attempt
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs and Splunk internal logs for file manipulation commands or syscalls originating from the sidecar process. Baseline expected file operations and alert on deviation or file writes outside normal configuration directories.

suggestion.title: Splunk: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk Enterprise's PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically high-numbered or service ports) that lack authentication headers or bearer tokens. Look for successful responses (200/201) to POST/PUT operations from external or low-privilege network segments. Correlate against Splunk vulnerability scanner results to confirm exposed instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk: Arbitrary File Creation via Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file I/O from unauthenticated service calls is anomalous and high-fidelity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk service process (splunkd, PostgreSQL sidecar) for unexpected file creation, truncation, or deletion operations targeting sensitive paths (/etc, /var/lib, configuration directories). Cross-reference with request logs to confirm timing alignment with sidecar endpoint access. Look for rapid batches of file modifications or deletion of critical application files.

suggestion.title: Splunk: File Truncation Causing Service Degradation
suggestion.rationale: Truncating arbitrary files could corrupt Splunk's internal state or logs, masking attack activity—'create or truncate arbitrary files' includes this impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file-integrity baselines for critical Splunk Enterprise files (config directories, index metadata, audit logs). Alert on unexpected truncations (file size drop to zero or significant reduction without maintenance window). Correlate truncation events with prior unauthenticated sidecar access to establish attack causality.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection on unauthorized access to Splunk's internal PostgreSQL listener.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for unexpected network connections to PostgreSQL sidecar service ports (typically 8191/TCP). Alert on authentication failures or missing credentials in connection attempts. Correlate with vulnerability scanner confirmations of CVE-2026-20253 presence.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Manipulation via PostgreSQL
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files' via PostgreSQL endpoint. File system operations on Splunk data/config directories initiated from network-based PostgreSQL queries are high-confidence indicators of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected file creation or truncation in Splunk Enterprise directories (var/lib/splunk, etc.) that correlate temporally with PostgreSQL process activity or sidecar service connections. Baseline normal Splunk file operations and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposed to Internet Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires unauthenticated network access. CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation, implying exposed instances are being actively scanned/exploited. Asset exposure detection is canonical for public-facing vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances with inbound internet routes and no authentication requirement. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Alert on any public-facing Splunk instances regardless of patch status.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Anomalous Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the attack surface as 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Queries to this internal service that attempt file operations (CREATE, DELETE) or attempt to execute OS commands are exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar service logs (typically at $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps) for queries containing file system operation patterns or unusual statement types. Splunk's sidecar is not meant to accept arbitrary SQL; any complex queries are anomalous.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user' to access PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint. No detection logic was generated despite this being the initial pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST/GET requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically port 5432 or sidecar REST API ports) from external networks or unauthenticated contexts. Baseline normal service-to-service traffic and flag anomalies. Use CVE-2026-20253 as query pivot.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the impact mechanism and should trigger file-system monitoring rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-system events from PostgreSQL service account (postgres, splunk_postgres) for unexpected creation or truncation of files outside expected data directories. Flag rapid file removal or zero-byte file overwrites.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry with federal patch due-date (2026-06-21). Pipeline should emit CVE as IOC for scanner pivot and patch-lag validation. This is standard for all CVE articles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20253 across Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference patch timestamps against published due-date (2026-06-21). Flag instances with evidence of exploitation (unusual sidecar access, file-operation anomalies) even if patched.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'unauthenticated user' access is the exploit path, implying network exposure. Standard asset-exposure hunt for Internet-facing Splunk instances should be generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external namespace (Shodan, Censys, passive DNS) for Splunk Enterprise ports (8089, 8000) and banner signatures. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unmanaged or shadow Splunk instances. Prioritize instances matching vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the attack vector is direct unauthenticated access to a critical service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS access logs for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (non-standard paths or ports) that lack valid authentication tokens, session IDs, or API keys, yet return success (2xx responses). Flag any caller issuing file-operation commands without credentials.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Creation via Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this impact must be detected via file-system monitoring correlated with unauthenticated endpoint activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation in sensitive Splunk directories (config, bin, var, indices) in temporal proximity to unauthenticated sidecar requests. Flag creation of files in unexpected paths or system-critical directories initiated outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Detect Log or Index File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'truncate arbitrary files'—attackers will destroy audit logs and indices to hide compromise. Truncation is a high-confidence post-exploitation cleanup indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for zero-byte files in Splunk index or log directories, or explicit truncate/delete operations on audit trails, index files, or configuration files. Alert immediately on any truncation of Splunk's own internal logs or audit indices.

suggestion.title: Network Scan for Exposed Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability requires the PostgreSQL sidecar to be exposed and reachable. Must establish baseline network exposure to identify at-risk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk deployments for PostgreSQL sidecar service listening on non-standard ports. Alert if service is reachable from external networks, internet-facing zones, or untrusted VLANs. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20253 patch status to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Authentication Control Bypass on Protected Splunk Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication for critical function'—this is a direct authentication control failure and must be observable via absence of required credentials on protected operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk protected endpoints (sidecar, admin interface) that succeed without authentication headers or with missing/invalid tokens returning 200-level responses. Establish baseline of authenticated requests and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatted Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious package was 'named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' No detection rule for confusable package names in Go dependency graphs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor go.mod updates and go get commands for packages with character-similarity typos against known legitimate packages (swap 'l' for '1', remove underscores, common OCR errors). Flag packages from unfamiliar registries pulling similar-named modules.

suggestion.title: Backdoored Dependency C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands i.e. via a command and control server.' No UC for outbound C2 from Go binaries post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from Go binaries compiled against known-clean boltdb. Flag new C2 domains/IPs contacted only after injection of malicious version; correlate with go.mod timestamp discontinuities (3-year gap before update).

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Module Cache Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module' persisting for 3+ years. No detection for stale cached versions diverging from upstream registry truth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference local go.sum checksums against Go Module Proxy metadata and upstream repo HEAD. Alert on cached module hashes not matching current upstream version for 6+ months; correlate with go version and build timestamps to identify systems still importing retired/poisoned versions.

suggestion.title: Long-Latency Dependency Update Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malicious version 'stayed in the system for 3 years' before updates: 'we now wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies.' Detect sudden bulk updates to dependency trees after years of stasis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag organizational waves of `go get -u` or `go mod tidy` across large dev/CI estate within short windows after no updates for 24+ months. Correlate with package-registry notifications (Jan 30 disclosure) and correlate with C2 communication spikes on affected systems in prior 3-year window.

suggestion.title: Mismatched Package Metadata vs. Binary Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article describes module 'went unnoticed for 3 years' despite hosting C2 code. No detection for packages whose declared functionality (embedded Go docs, CHANGELOG) diverge from actual binary behavior (network beaconing, process execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For high-risk packages (crypto, database, HTTP), perform behavioral analysis on imported binaries: static string scanning for C2 strings, outbound socket initialization, syscall patterns. Compare against package documentation and legitimate upstream. Flag packages exhibiting undocumented I/O or network behavior.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Registry Poisoning Detection via Source Integrity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Module was cached on Go Module Proxy, which continued to serve clients' despite removal from GitHub. Detect divergence between GitHub source and registry-cached binary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate Go module hashes (go.sum) against both Go Module Proxy AND GitHub source tree. Alert when Proxy-cached hash does not match any GitHub commit hash; correlate with timestamp gaps between GitHub removal and proxy scrubbing. Monitor for tools fetching modules from mirrors only after primary source deletion.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack entry point; pipeline produced no authentication-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated connection attempts to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint (internal service port). Correlate external or non-service-account sources attempting POST/PUT requests to vulnerable endpoints with CVE-2026-20253 signature patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit outcome as 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File integrity and process-level detection entirely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation or sudden size reduction of Splunk config, audit, and data directories originating from PostgreSQL sidecar processes. Alert on file deletion/truncation following failed-auth attempts to sidecar within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal patch due-date 2026-06-21 (now past). Pipeline must surface unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances as critical compliance gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Splunk Enterprise instances with versions prior to patched release for CVE-2026-20253. Flag any instances still unpatched past due-date as critical risk. Cross-reference with network accessibility scans to identify externally-exposed vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Endpoint External Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint to be reachable by unauthenticated users, implying potential external accessibility. Pipeline generated no network-exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk hosts with PostgreSQL sidecar port (internal service) reachable from internet or untrusted networks. Alert if inbound traffic reaches Splunk service ports from external subnets without VPN/bastion authentication context.

suggestion.title: Splunk Audit Log Integrity Degradation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation capability creates immediate risk of audit-log destruction post-exploitation. Article does not name this explicitly, but 'truncate arbitrary files' on a Splunk instance threatens audit visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for unexplained gaps, backwards time progression, or sudden file-size reduction in audit directories. Alert on missing audit entries corresponding to sidecar authentication-bypass attempts or file-operation events.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct authentication bypass surface. This is the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instance logs for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically non-standard ports, paths containing 'sidecar' or 'postgres'). Baseline legitimate sidecar clients and alert on any requests from external IP ranges or without valid Splunk auth tokens. CISA KEV indicates this is already exploited in the wild.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the exploitation capability—this is the destructive impact phase that detections must capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification events in process chain where Splunk processes (splunkd, postgres sidecars) create files outside expected data directories (check vendor documentation for expected write paths). Flag any file writes to /etc, /var, or other sensitive locations. Correlate with the sidecar endpoint access hunt.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'truncate arbitrary files'—file deletion/truncation could indicate log tampering, evidence removal, or system degradation attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file truncation (size→0) or deletion events originating from Splunk service accounts or child processes of splunkd. Cross-reference with timeline of sidecar endpoint access; truncations immediately following unauthorized requests indicate exploitation. Particularly sensitive: audit logs, system logs, application logs.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Network Connections to PostgreSQL from Splunk Instance
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow requires reaching 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—unauthenticated requests will come from external network if sidecar is exposed. Monitor for unexpected inbound or lateral connections to database ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected PostgreSQL connections to Splunk instances (should be internal, from named hosts). Alert on connections from external sources, non-whitelisted internal IPs, or any connection attempts to the sidecar port that do not complete the TLS handshake or send authentication headers. CVE-2026-20253 exploits *missing* auth, so unauthenticated connections are the red flag.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Vulnerability Scanner / Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV, indicating active exploitation. Standard practice is asset inventory and scanner correlation. Ensure all Splunk Enterprise instances are enumerated and checked against CVE-2026-20253.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query your vulnerability scanner for 'CVE-2026-20253' or 'Splunk Enterprise' instances with missing auth checks on PostgreSQL sidecar. Cross-reference with internet-facing assets (public IPs, DNS-resolvable hostnames, cloud ingress). Any unpatched Splunk instance exposed before patch date 2026-06-21 is high-priority incident. Check patch lag on all instances; CISA KEV indicates you are behind by the time you read this.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Sidecar Service Access (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct exploitation vector requiring detection of unauthorized service endpoint calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints for HTTP requests lacking valid authentication (missing session tokens, BASIC auth, or API keys). suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt'; pipeline provided no scanner-based detection logic to identify CVE-2026-20253 impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory or version-detection logs for Splunk Enterprise builds prior to patched version. Cross-reference with network exposure scanning (Shodan, internal port scans) to identify instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Critical-Function API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function'; the article does not specify which API endpoints, yet this is the core exploitation mechanic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs and HTTP access logs for requests to /services/ API endpoints (file, data, input, output endpoints) lacking valid authorization tokens, session cookies, or X-Splunk-Authorization headers. Flag anonymous or default-credential patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE ID is the primary IOC for a CISA KEV entry; no use case was generated to detect active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk instances for known exploit payloads or patterns targeting PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (e.g., encoded file paths, sidecar-service URIs) and correlate with failed authentication logs and subsequent file-modification events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Scanner Detection + Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry observed in wild; 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-21'. Standard asset-exposure hunt for critical CVEs—scan output followed by manual patch check for lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Splunk Enterprise instances in scanner output matching CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with asset inventory patch status. Prioritize instances updated *after* 2026-06-21 (lag indicator).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Detection gap: no hunt for unauthenticated requests to sidecar endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests (likely 5432-range or Splunk management port) to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking authentication headers or valid session tokens. Flag non-200 or 403 responses indicating auth bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'. Attack surface is file-system writes—no file-operation detection UC provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk Enterprise processes (or postgresql sidecar) creating/truncating files outside expected paths (/opt/splunk, /var/lib/pgsql). Flag truncations of log files, configuration files, or system binaries as high-severity.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: T1190 requires public-facing application. Article implies external access to sidecar endpoint; missing external-exposure baseline hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk management/sidecar ports (8089, 5432-range) accessible from untrusted CIDR blocks (WAN, guest networks). Correlate with outbound exploit traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Process Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. No behavioral UC for sidecar process abuse (unexpected spawns, privilege escalation, network connections).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PostgreSQL sidecar process spawning unexpected child processes, making unauthorized network connections, or escalating privileges. Flag deviations from baseline sidecar behavior.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — endpoint exposure on network-accessible ports is the direct attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP/HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise hosts targeting PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or custom variants) from untrusted sources or external origins. Flag unauthenticated connection attempts as exploitation attempts for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Operations via Splunk Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — successful exploitation manifests as anomalous file system operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create/delete/truncate operations on Splunk Enterprise hosts lacking corresponding authenticated user activity or matching known CVE-2026-20253 attack patterns. Correlate file system events with unauthenticated endpoint access logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Version Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with published date 2026-06-18 and federal patch due 2026-06-21 signals active exploitation; article references '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' template confirming detection is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and software inventory for Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with asset management to identify exposed instances; prioritize externally-facing or DMZ-resident systems.

suggestion.title: Authentication-Bypass Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability title 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function' indicates core flaw: absent auth checks on normally-protected endpoints; detect unauthenticated calls to critical APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise API endpoints for critical functions (file operations, configuration, data access) that lack valid authentication credentials (bearer token, session cookie, API key) or carry known bypass payloads. Correlate with source reputation and geolocation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files'—initial access vector entirely undetected by pipeline. Requires hunt against Splunk access logs for auth-bypass or missing-auth patterns on file operation endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Splunk access logs for successful requests to critical file-operation endpoints from sessions lacking valid authentication tokens or showing auth_status=failed immediately followed by auth_status=success (credential replay). Establish baseline of authenticated users; flag unauthenticated requests to /_<file_op_endpoint>.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack surface: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No detection generated despite this being the direct exploitation vector for file manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or custom bound port) from external/untrusted sources. Alert on POST/PUT requests to sidecar endpoints lacking expected authentication headers. Correlate with Splunk audit logs showing file operations initiated from sidecar without credentials.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Creation/Truncation by Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Detection pipeline generated no file-system monitoring use case despite this being the observable exploitation result.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation events from Splunk service account (splunk/splunkd process). Alert on operations targeting system-sensitive paths (/etc/, /var/log/, application binaries) or batch file truncation patterns. Baseline expected Splunk file operations in normal directories; flag deviation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article with federal patch deadline (2026-06-21). Pipeline failed to generate vulnerability scanning or asset-exposure hunt despite article body explicitly recommending this via template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results (Nessus, Qualys, OpenVAS) for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with patch management to verify remediation before federal deadline. Alert on any instances still vulnerable past 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration/Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'missing authentication'—attack depends on bypassing or circumventing auth controls. Pipeline generated no detection for auth-bypass patterns or config-file manipulation that could indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Splunk audit logs for failed authentication attempts followed by successful sensitive operations (file creation/deletion) in short time windows. Monitor for authentication config changes (auth.conf modifications, SSO bypass). Flag requests with malformed or missing auth headers that succeed instead of failing.

suggestion.title: Langflow RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Langflow RCE'—a public-facing application vulnerability being exploited. Pipeline did not surface initial-access detection for RCE payloads or web requests targeting known Langflow CVEs (e.g., path traversal, code injection endpoints).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Langflow endpoints (/api, /flow, /execute) with suspicious payloads (shell metacharacters, Python exec, curl/wget). Correlate with web server errors (500, 403) or successful connection logs followed by high-privilege process spawn.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python/Node Process Execution from Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI Agent Exploits Langflow RCE to Automate'—Langflow likely executes Python or Node code; RCE gains execution context. Pipeline did not flag process creation from web service identity (www-data, nobody, IIS AppPool).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python3/python or node process spawns originating from Langflow service PID or network-accessible Python interpreter startup with inline code (-c, -m flags) or suspicious module imports (subprocess, os.system, psutil). Baseline expected code execution.

suggestion.title: Database Ransomware Activity Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Database Ransomware Attack'—pipeline did not surface detection for encryption, backup deletion, or mass file modification on database storage (MSSQL data files, PostgreSQL tablespaces, MySQL InnoDB). Core impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .mdf, .ldf, .ibd, .fdb files being opened by non-database-service processes for write; batch file deletion (DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, rm -rf); rapid sequential encryption-like file extension changes (.sql → .locked/.crypt); or database service restart anomalies post-exploit.

suggestion.title: AI Agent / Automated Ransomware Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'AI Agent Exploits...to Automate'—suggests scripting/agent framework (Python async, bash loops, Golang binary). Pipeline did not detect automated payload delivery or multi-step attack orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell/Python scripts spawning multiple database-targeting commands (sqlmap, xp_cmdshell, mysql -h, psql -U) in rapid succession, or encoded/obfuscated scripts (base64, hex) detonated from /tmp, /dev/shm, or suspicious download locations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Langflow Instance
suggestion.rationale: RCE into Langflow → database server often requires network pivot. Article does not specify Langflow and DB on same host. Pipeline missed detection for east-west reconnaissance (port scanning, service enumeration) from the web server VLAN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Langflow RCE compromise with subsequent failed/successful connections to database ports (3306, 5432, 1433) from the web server; flag port scanning (SYN timeout patterns) or unusual outbound SMB/SSH from web tier to backend infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Langflow Service Abuse for C2 / Persistence Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article title does not explicitly mention C2, but automated AI agent implies malware or persistence mechanism. Langflow could be weaponized to phone home, download payloads, or maintain backdoor. Pipeline produced zero C2-detection IOCs or beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Langflow process making outbound HTTPS connections to non-whitelisted domains; look for POST requests with JSON payloads (exfiltrated data) or PE/ELF binary downloads to /tmp. Correlate DNS queries and SSL certificate chains for known malware C2 or bulletproof hosting.

suggestion.title: Multi-Year Crypto Miner Persistence on Domain Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Case study explicitly: 'Four-year-old crypto mining activity on domain controllers' — represents critical detection gap for dormant SYSTEM-level persistence not caught by endpoint protection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on crypto-pool domain connections (stratum, getwork protocols) from SYSTEM context processes on domain controllers persisting across reboots. Flag long-lived scheduled tasks or registry run keys executing unsigned miners with consistent outbound pattern.

suggestion.title: In-Memory Malware Bypassing Endpoint Protection
suggestion.rationale: Two case studies: 'In-memory PurpleFox infection evades conventional endpoint protection' and 'In-memory LionTail infection on critical Windows servers' — defense evasion via process injection defeating file-based detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injection chains: benign parent (svchost, explorer) + WriteVirtualMemory API + abnormal child process or network behavior without corresponding on-disk binary. Correlate unsigned DLL loads into system processes with C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LoLBins and Remote Management Tool Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Section header: 'Legitimate, yet suspicious: LoLBins and remote management tools' — indicates abuse of LOLBins for execution and remote tools for lateral movement in assessed compromises
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell spawning from unexpected parents (SYSTEM services, Office processes), or psexec/RDP sessions immediately followed by data staging or reconnaissance commands. Anomalize remote management tool usage by hour/user/destination.

suggestion.title: Dormant Malware Reactivation After Extended Dormancy
suggestion.rationale: Case study title: 'Dormant threat uncovered only by a compromise assessment' and 'Unintentional malware preservation' — malware inactive for weeks/months then re-executing, evading behavior-based detection windows
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of files with creation timestamps >30 days old, especially combined with decompression/decoding actions (certutil, 7zip, PowerShell ExpandArchive). Correlate with network callbacks to previously unseen C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GPO-Based Enterprise Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'How overly permissive GPO-based software distribution goes wrong' — malware deployed at scale via Group Policy for persistent domain-wide compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SYSVOL for unauthorized executable additions to Group Policy logon/startup scripts. Alert on mass simultaneous execution of unsigned binaries from GPO paths across domain members, especially those connecting to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Access and Discovery Without Early Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Missed long-term incidents' where threats remained undetected despite years of presence — suggests credential harvesting and reconnaissance phases preceding actual data theft or impact
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rare failed logon attempts from a single source to domain controllers/SQL servers with successful logons using compromised accounts weeks later. Flag LSASS access from unsigned tools and multi-target enumeration (net user, whoami, dsquery).

suggestion.title: MFA Bombing / MFA Fatigue Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'targeted multi-factor authentication (MFA) bombing (aka MFA fatigue)' as Scattered Spider's signature technique; this is their primary credential-access vector yet no detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users receiving ≥10 MFA challenges within 5 minutes, especially when followed by successful authentication from a new device, IP, or geography. Correlate with credential-reset events within 1–6 hours. Flag accounts targeted multiple times in a 24-hour window as potential fatigue attacks.

suggestion.title: Helpdesk-Initiated Credential Reset Followed by Anomalous Admin Logon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes May 2025 attack: 'hackers allegedly called the company's IT helpdesk, posing as employees, to reset credentials and gain access to administrator accounts.' This social-engineering–to–privilege-escalation chain is the attack's pivot point; no detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alert when a credential reset via helpdesk/support is followed (within 2–8 hours) by an administrator-account logon from a new IP, VPN, or ASN. Correlate with helpdesk call/ticket metadata to identify anomalous reset requests (e.g., after-hours, unusual requester patterns, foreign IP origin).

suggestion.title: Genymobile Android Emulator Deployment on Corporate Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'they commonly use the Genymobile Android emulator during their MFA attacks.' This is a specific, detectable artifact used to simulate SMS receipt and intercept OTP codes; no tooling-detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or installation of Genymobile emulator, Android emulator binaries, or related virtualization tools on corporate endpoints, especially from user-writable directories or following suspicious download activity. Monitor emulator processes for network connections to MFA services, SMS gateways, or credential-management endpoints.

suggestion.title: DragonForce Ransomware Encryptor Execution – Scattered Spider Post-Exfil Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Scattered Spider 'deployed DragonForce encryptor in ransomware attacks against UK retail companies.' No impact-phase detection was generated for this specific encryptor malware or file-encryption behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DragonForce encryptor execution or file-system encryption signatures; alert on bulk sequential file modifications with encryption-like entropy patterns, especially post-exfiltration. Correlate with data-staging indicators (large file copies to removable media or staging directories) and known Scattered Spider IOCs.

suggestion.title: SMS Phishing for Credential Harvesting – Scattered Spider Pre-Attack Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'SMS credential phishing attacks to steal user credentials' as core to Scattered Spider's initial compromise. Pipeline generated no detection for SMS-based phishing or out-of-band credential-theft channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SMS messages or out-of-band communications containing login-portal URLs or credential-capture links. Correlate SMS delivery timestamps with subsequent authentication attempts from new devices/IPs or failed credential-entry events (indicating phishing confirmation). Cross-reference with known Scattered Spider phishing domains.

suggestion.title: FortiBleed Public-Facing Application Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes FortiBleed as the attack vector ('FortiBleed Credential Theft'). A vulnerability in a public-facing application (Fortinet appliance) being exploited for initial access is the entry point; pipeline should detect anomalous HTTP requests, authentication bypass patterns, or WAF triggers on FortiGate/Fortinet endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet appliance logs and upstream network telemetry for request patterns consistent with CVE exploitation (unusual HTTP methods, path traversal attempts, authentication endpoint abuse). Correlate with known FortiBleed PoC signatures or suspicious SSL certificate chains.

suggestion.title: Credential Access and Exfiltration via FortiBleed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Credential Theft' and links to ransomware operations, indicating attackers are harvesting credentials post-exploitation. Pipeline should detect mass credential queries, password-store access, or auth-log anomalies on affected systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious reads from credential stores (SAM, LSASS memory dumps, Windows vault), unusual authentication failures followed by successes from the same source, or SAM/LSA process injection on Fortinet-managed or adjacent systems.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using FortiBleed-Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article links FortiBleed to INC and Lynx ransomware—both groups are known for lateral movement after initial compromise. Stolen credentials enable reconnaissance and pivot. Pipeline should detect use of harvested credentials for anomalous admin logons or cross-segment access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for admin-account usage (e.g., Domain Admin, service accounts) originating from non-admin hosts or at atypical times; cross-reference against FortiBleed exploitation timeframes. Detect lateral SMB/RDP traffic to high-value targets (domain controllers, file servers) within 1-24 hours of suspected initial compromise.

suggestion.title: INC and Lynx Ransomware Post-Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article names two specific threat actors—INC and Lynx Ransomware—by reputation linked to post-breach encryption and extortion. Pipeline should detect their known tools, C2 signatures, or domain/IP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query threat-intel feeds for INC and Lynx C2 domains, IP addresses, and file signatures. Alert on DNS requests to known C2, network beacons to observed threat-actor infrastructure, or execution of known ransomware payloads (e.g., via hash, yara, command-line patterns).

suggestion.title: FortiBleed Exploitation Detection via Fortinet Log Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on FortiBleed vulnerability. Fortinet appliances log authentication, admin access, and system events; pipeline should extract and alert on abnormal patterns specific to compromised appliances (e.g., unauthorized admin creation, privilege-escalation logs, configuration changes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet appliance logs for creation of new admin accounts, privilege escalations, or changes to firewall rules immediately following FortiBleed exploitation signature or timeframe. Cross-correlate with upstream packet captures for anomalous SSL sessions or HTTP abuse.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Execution from Repository Clone Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake PoC exploit repos' — researchers clone and execute scripts. Missing detection for when scripts execute from .git, downloads, or temp directories tied to repo operations (e.g., `git clone` followed by python/powershell execution in <1 min).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of .py, .ps1, or compiled binaries from user Downloads, AppData\Local\Temp, or directories matching git clone patterns within 2 minutes of git/wget activity. Researcher accounts (vulnerability analysis tools in profile) are higher priority.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing Post-Repository Execution
suggestion.rationale: RAT implies command-and-control callbacks. Article states malware 'targets' researchers but does not detail C2 mechanism — pipeline should surface detection for suspicious outbound connections to non-standard ports or known C2 ASNs post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections to IPs/domains NOT in approved researcher tool-download whitelists (GitHub, GitLab, PyPI, etc.) originating from the execution-parent process. Look for long-lived TCP sessions (beaconing) to port ranges atypical for HTTPS.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Enumeration or Credential Access Post-RAT Execution
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically conduct discovery and credential harvesting ('targets vulnerability researchers' implies data of value to attackers). Missing detection for unusual file-system enumeration or access to .ssh, .git/config, browser credential stores post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by or child-of suspicious script execution accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, credential managers, or git config files. Cross-reference with researcher personas (security tools, vuln research binaries in AppData).

suggestion.title: Repository Metadata Tampering or Suspicious .git/ Access
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed detection for the 'fake PoC repo' stage itself. If organizations scan commits or verify repo authenticity, missing detection for git object manipulation, commit-author spoofing, or .git/config exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cloning of repositories from domains recently registered or with short domain age, OR git operations reading .git/config outside of normal IDE/tool context, OR commits authored by accounts with low reputation/activity-history on those platforms.

suggestion.title: Memory Injection or Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: RATs require persistence. Article does not specify mechanism, but pipeline should generate UC for hallmark RAT persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI, process injection). 'Fake PoC' is initial vector; persistence is the exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to Run, RunOnce, or HKCU persistence keys within 5 minutes of suspicious script execution. Flag unsigned DLLs loaded by python.exe or powershell.exe, or scheduled tasks created by non-admin users executing from temp/downloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Researcher Workstations to Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: High-value target (researchers) suggests attackers may pivot to internal resources (source code repos, vulnerability databases, secrets). Missing UC for unusual internal reconnaissance post-RAT compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised researcher workstations scanning internal IP ranges (169.254 sweep), enumerating network shares (\\\\, net view), or connecting to internal git/secret servers (GitHub Enterprise, internal artifact repos) from non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Typo-Squatting Package Installation in Go Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malicious Go Module Mirror's was named github.com/botdb-go/bolt, similar to the original one i.e. github.com/boltdb/bolt.' Pipeline should detect go.mod/go.sum imports of near-identical package names to known popular modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for go get, go mod, and import statements pulling packages with names phonetically or visually similar to popular Go packages (edit-distance ≤2 from canonical names). Cross-reference against Go Module Proxy advisory lists and Socket research datasets. Flag mismatches between expected package maintainer (e.g., boltdb org vs. botdb-go org).

suggestion.title: Persistent Malicious Package Installation via Go Module Mirror Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Go Module Mirror service stored it permanently' and 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' Detection needed for exploit of cache persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a Go application loads a module from a Go Module Proxy/cache after the module's upstream source has been removed or reverted. Cross-check module versions pulled from local cache against Go Vulnerability Database and official mirrors; flag version mismatches or cached modules flagged as malicious post-installation.

suggestion.title: C2 Command & Control via Compromised Go Package Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' No detection hypothesis for C2 communication from BoltDB-using applications was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from processes linked to Go applications that have imported the malicious botdb-go/bolt package (v1.3.1). Look for outbound connections to known/unknown C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS queries, or suspicious HTTP/HTTPS traffic patterns characteristic of command injection (suspicious User-Agent, POST to atypical endpoints, exfiltration-like payloads).

suggestion.title: Lateral Dependency Update Triggering Installation of Stale Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Developers unknowingly updated to the backdoored version when refreshing dependencies, suggesting detection around unexpected dependency version changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when developers or CI/CD pipelines run go get -u or go mod tidy and the resulting go.mod pins a package version that has been flagged in vulnerability databases or removed from upstream mirrors. Correlate with Socket/Snyk/Go vulnerability feeds. Alert if a module was unavailable/removed but resurfaces in local cache.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Go Module Dependency on Backdoored Package (github.com/botdb-go/bolt)
suggestion.rationale: The package name github.com/botdb-go/bolt and version 1.3.1 are IOCs that should trigger detection when discovered in build artifacts or runtime imports. Article confirms 'impacted thousands of organizations for over three years.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any go.mod, go.sum, or Dockerfile containing dependency on github.com/botdb-go/bolt (all versions, especially 1.3.1). Cross-correlate with SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841 and GO-2025-3451 CVE/advisory records. Alert on presence in source control, container images, and runtime process introspection.

suggestion.title: Go Module Mirror Cache Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies a systemic weakness: 'There have been over 80+ unresolved issues in the original repository since 2015' and 'Malicious packages can still be searchable on Go Module Proxy.' Detection needed for cache-based persistence exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to Go Module Proxy or pkg.go.dev for packages that have been flagged as removed, reverted, or malicious. Detect when a Go build system fetches a module version that does not exist or differs in hash/checksum from the canonical upstream source. Flag version-pinning strategies that bypass security checks or pull from cache without validation.

suggestion.title: Langflow Remote Code Execution Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'exploits Langflow RCE'—direct evidence of CVE exploitation against Langflow application. Pipeline missed the named vulnerability entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Langflow API endpoints (/api/flows, /api/chat, /api/components) with payload sizes exceeding baseline; correlate with unexpected child process spawning (shell, Python, bash) from Langflow runtime process.

suggestion.title: AI Framework Spawning Database Encryption Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'AI Agent... to Automate Database Ransomware'—indicates parent process (Python/Node-based AI framework) launching encryption binaries or database tools. No UC for this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent process matching AI/LLM framework signatures (langchain, llama-index, crew.py) spawning children: encryption utilities (openssl, gpg, cryptsetup), database tools (mysql, psql, sqlcmd), or generic shell interpreters with file I/O patterns.

suggestion.title: Mass Database File Encryption Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Database Ransomware Attack'—attack culminates in encryption of database files. Pipeline missed the impact phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file creation/modification in database directories (Program Files\*\data, /var/lib/mysql, /var/lib/postgresql) with ransom-typical extensions (.locked, .encrypted, .ransom, .nomoreaccess) or inode changes indicating in-place encryption.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance to Database Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: AI agent must discover database targets across network before encryption. Article: 'Automate Database Ransomware'—implies scanning/discovery phase not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scanning patterns from compromised host post-RCE: sequential connection attempts to common database ports (3306 MySQL, 5432 PostgreSQL, 1433 MSSQL, 27017 MongoDB) across subnet ranges, especially with low response times and high failure rate.

suggestion.title: Langflow Configuration File Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE attacker would harvest Langflow config (.env, secrets.yaml, database credentials) to understand available APIs and flows. Article mentions automation via AI Agent—requires config knowledge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process reads of Langflow-specific config files and environment variable access during/after RCE exploitation window; correlate with suspicious outbound HTTPS/DNS indicative of credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Langflow Service Account to Database Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Automate Database Ransomware Attack'—implies lateral movement from initial RCE foothold (Langflow host) to database infrastructure. No UC for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from Langflow process/host to database servers using credentials harvested from config; look for pass-the-hash or Kerberos ticket reuse patterns and SMB/RDP logon sequences from service account.

suggestion.title: Dormant Crypto Miner Activation on Domain Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'Four-year-old crypto mining activity on domain controllers' remained undetected. Article emphasizes 'missed long-term incidents' and mining as persistent threat on critical infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain controllers for CPU-intensive processes with sustained network connections to mining pool domains/IPs (stratum protocol). Detect process patterns indicating dormant binaries (low execution frequency, parent process reuse). Baseline legitimate DC activity and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: In-Memory Fileless Malware Injection (PurpleFox Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'In-memory PurpleFox infection evades conventional endpoint protection.' Article identifies fileless/in-memory infection as undetected threat category requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cross-process code injection via VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + SetWindowsHookEx chains. Monitor for suspicious API call patterns on host processes (explorer.exe, svchost.exe). Correlate with rare/unsigned DLL injection and unusual memory protections.

suggestion.title: LionTail Backdoor Persistence on Critical Servers
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'In-memory LionTail infection on critical Windows servers' as persistence mechanism. Article emphasizes detection gaps for backdoors on infrastructure targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor critical servers for LionTail registration: suspicious HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entries, scheduled tasks with encoded payloads, AppInit_DLLs modifications, service account changes. Flag non-standard registry persistence on servers with low change frequency.

suggestion.title: LoLBins-based Execution with Suspicious Command Lines
suggestion.rationale: Article tags and body highlight 'Legitimate, yet suspicious: LoLBins and remote management tools' as detection gap. Discusses weaponization of legitimate tools (PowerShell, wmic.exe, certutil.exe).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous LoLBins execution: PowerShell with -EncodedCommand/-NoProfile from unusual parents; wmic.exe spawning cmd/powershell; certutil.exe with -decode; bitsadmin.exe with /transfer and suspicious URLs. Establish baseline for each tool per department; alert on command-line indicators of code execution or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload and Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article tags reference 'web shell' as initial compromise vector. Case study 'How overly permissive GPO-based software distribution goes wrong' implies web-accessible services targeted. No detection provided for web shell persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web-accessible directories for suspicious uploads (*.asp*, *.php, *.jsp, *.cgi). Correlate with w3wp.exe/apache spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe. Detect HTTP POST requests to admin paths with executable payloads. Flag inbound connections followed by unusual process creation on web servers.

suggestion.title: Group Policy Object Exploitation for Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'How overly permissive GPO-based software distribution goes wrong' identifies GPO as attack vector. Article discusses root cause as 'Insufficient vulnerability management' in distribution infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit GPO modifications (DS replication changes, unexpected Group Policy Object creation). Detect SYSVOL updates pointing to suspicious software distribution packages. Monitor for domain-joined systems executing unsigned/untrusted binaries immediately after GPO refresh. Flag unauthorized SoftwareDistributionPoint entries.

suggestion.title: FortiBleed Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'FortiBleed Credential Theft' as the initial attack vector linking to both INC and Lynx. Pipeline missed the primary exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Fortinet FortiOS logs for suspicious HTTP requests to known FortiBleed-vulnerable endpoints, anomalous SSL/TLS handshakes, and WAF bypass attempts. Correlate exploitation timestamps with subsequent credential-access and lateral-movement activity.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Credential Extraction from FortiBleed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'credential theft' as the attack outcome but pipeline missed credential-access-phase detections despite this being central to the threat chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exfiltration of Fortinet admin credentials, keystore materials, or cached authentication tokens. Monitor for unusual authentication patterns post-exploitation: failed logins from external IP ranges, credential-spray patterns, and out-of-hours access using service accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Fortinet Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Stolen Fortinet credentials are the leverage for ransomware group access to internal networks. Pipeline missed the lateral-movement phase despite its criticality to INC/Lynx operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logon events from compromised Fortinet accounts at unusual times or from unexpected geographies. Flag RDP and SMB sessions originating from recently-compromised admin accounts. Cross-correlate with credential-access alerts within 24–48 hours.

suggestion.title: INC/Lynx Ransomware Execution Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes operational link to INC and Lynx ransomware but pipeline generated zero detections for payload execution, encryption, or system modification phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass file encryption (high entropy writes, .locked or .lynx extensions), registry modifications (HKCU/HKLM boot-sector tampering), and process chains typical of INC/Lynx (wmic.exe, powershell.exe invoking cryptography libraries, vssadmin.exe deletion).

suggestion.title: INC/Lynx Command-and-Control Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references INC and Lynx ransomware operations but pipeline missed network-based C2 indicators and beaconing patterns typical of these groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network traffic to known INC/Lynx C2 infrastructure. Monitor for beaconing (periodic outbound connections), DNS queries to suspicious domains, and SSL/TLS certificate anomalies. Detect peer-to-peer or Tor exit-node connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub/GitLab Repo Clone from Security Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware distributed via 'Fake PoC Exploit Repos'—researchers would clone these using git or web browser. Pipeline should detect clones of newly-created or spoofed repository names containing keywords like 'exploit', 'poc', 'cve' targeting security research tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git.exe, git-bash, or curl/wget activity targeting GitHub/GitLab domains with repo paths containing exploit/PoC keywords. Flag repositories created within 7 days or with zero stars/forks but sudden clone activity. Correlate with security researcher tool process chains (burp, metasploit, ghidra).

suggestion.title: Execution of RAT Payload from Archive Downloaded from Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article implies researchers download fake PoC code and execute it. Pipeline should detect archive extraction (7z, zip, rar) followed by execution of scripts or binaries with RAT-like behavioral signatures (network communication, persistence setup).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process chains: explorer/7-zip/WinRAR → extraction of .py/.ps1/.exe → immediate network egress or registry write. Flag Python/PowerShell execution from %TEMP% or Downloads folders with obfuscated base64 or suspicious module imports (socket, threading, ctypes for process injection).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing Post-RAT Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChocoPoC as a RAT—implies command-and-control communication.
