Correlate with subsequent successful authentication or API calls from 9router to that provider using those credentials, especially if provider is high-privilege (internal service, database, secret manager).

suggestion.title: Python eval()/exec() with LLM-generated code execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'When these agents evaluate LLM-generated tool messages with full_eval=True'—the core vulnerability is dynamic code evaluation. This is the exploitation phase; currently undetected. No hunt for eval(), exec(), compile(), or __import__() calls with untrusted input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes calling eval, exec, or compile with argument strings originating from network input, tool outputs, or LLM integration points. Correlate child process spawning immediately after eval/exec calls to identify post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Exploit public-facing Langroid API with malicious tool messages (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 but no UC hunts the initial exploitation. Vulnerability is triggered via 'LLM-generated tool messages' fed to TableChatAgent/VectorStore. Missing detection for malicious crafted messages or unusual agent input patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langroid TableChatAgent and VectorStore query logs for messages containing eval(), exec(), subprocess keywords, or code syntax. Correlate with unusual Python process spawning or multi-stage eval patterns within seconds of tool message ingestion.

suggestion.title: Tool transfer and staging post-RCE (T1105 — Ingress Tool Transfer)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1105 as technique but no UC hunts for tool downloads. RCE payload typically stages secondary tools. Missing detection for curl/wget initiated by child shells to fetch payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag curl/wget/PowerShell downloads spawned from Python or shell children, especially to ephemeral paths (/tmp, %TEMP%), with executable or script extensions, or from suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: VectorStore eval() injection via malicious vector queries
suggestion.rationale: Article names VectorStore as vulnerable but no UC addresses vector query evaluation. Missing detection for eval() or filter operations on LLM-generated query strings within VectorStore operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python VectorStore query/filter/search calls that invoke eval() with untrusted query content. Monitor for code-injection patterns in vector filter expressions or query metadata parsed as code.

suggestion.title: Symlink/hardlink creation by archive-extraction processes targeting paths outside extraction root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'A link (hardlink) or symlink entry is created without checking where its target points.' This is the core attack vector but no detection hunt addresses symlink/hardlink creation itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink (ln -s) or hardlink (ln) creation by archive utilities (node, tar, unzip, 7z) where link target contains parent-directory traversal (..) or absolute paths (/etc, /root, /usr) outside declared extraction directory.

suggestion.title: Cron/systemd script execution following archive extraction to /etc/cron.* or /etc/systemd/system
suggestion.rationale: Article describes writing to cron and systemd paths (—these enable persistence, but pipeline detects only the write, not activation. Article: writes to '/etc/cron.d/*', '/etc/cron.hourly/*', '/etc/systemd/system/*' are escalation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DeviceFileEvents (cron/systemd file creation by node) with DeviceProcessEvents showing execution of scripts in those paths within 5 minutes, with no legitimate package-manager parent process.

suggestion.title: Setuid/ld.so.preload-based privilege escalation following node-driven archive extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1548.001 and T1574.006 as techniques but provides no detection for the *exploitation* phase: pipeline detects file writes to /etc/ld.so.preload but not subsequent binary execution that loads it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when process execution follows write to /etc/ld.so.preload or /usr/local/sbin (written by node) within 2 minutes, especially if the executed binary shows privilege escalation artifacts (UID change, capability gain).

suggestion.title: SSH authorized_keys or sudoers.d file injection via archive extraction by unprivileged node process
suggestion.rationale: UC_5_2 monitors these paths but doesn't distinguish between legitimate system updates and malicious injection. Article: attacker-controlled archives write to '/.ssh/authorized_keys', '/etc/sudoers.d/*'—these are direct-access persistence vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modification to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or /etc/sudoers.d/* by node/nodejs process running as unprivileged user (not root, not system service accounts). Baseline on approved SSH key management tools.

suggestion.title: Cavern C2 Command-and-Control Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'new Cavern C2 Framework' as the attack vehicle. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no C2-phase kill-chain. Detecting beacon traffic to known C2 infrastructure is the primary defensive value from this article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS outbound connections to known Cavern C2 domains and IP addresses, particularly on non-standard ports. Look for beaconing patterns: regular, small-payload requests to the same C2 host with consistent User-Agent strings and encrypted body content.

suggestion.title: Iran-Linked Spear Phishing and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Iran-linked APT groups (APT33, APT34, etc.) invariably use spear-phishing for initial access; article references 'targeting Israeli organizations' implying targeted delivery. No initial-access detection logic generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with .exe, .scr, .lnk, or macro-enabled Office attachments sent to Israeli defense, government, or critical infrastructure sectors. Correlate sender domain reputation, domain age, and SPF/DKIM alignment. Watch for credential-harvesting landing pages spoofing Israeli organization portals.

suggestion.title: Cavern C2 Process Injection and Memory Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Typical Iran APT tradecraft involves process hollowing/injection (T1543, T1055) to evade EDR; no execution-phase detection or technique mapping by pipeline despite 'framework' language implying sophisticated post-exploitation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/anomalous child processes spawned by legitimate system processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe, explorer.exe). Flag processes with parent-child mismatch (e.g., csrss.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe) and unusual DLL loads in System32 contexts.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence: Run Key and Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: Iran-linked APTs establish persistence via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and Scheduled Tasks; no persistence-phase kill-chain generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of new Registry values in Run/RunOnce keys and HKCU startup folders, especially with randomized names or obfuscated paths. Alert on Scheduled Task creation with suspicious triggers (logon, system startup) or Task XML containing encoded/base64 payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Kerberoasting and SMB Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Iran APTs enumerate domain trusts and exploit Kerberos; article states targeting 'Israeli organizations' (likely domain-joined networks) but pipeline reconstructed zero lateral-movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TGS requests (Event ID 4769) with unusual service accounts and RC4 encryption. Alert on failed SMB authentication storms (4625 events) followed by successful logon (4624) on non-standard hours, indicating credential stuffing followed by lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Over Encrypted C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article's focus on 'Israeli organizations' implies targeting of sensitive data; pipeline failed to generate exfiltration-phase detection despite T1041 being standard for C2 frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline organizational network egress and alert on anomalous outbound data volumes to new external IPs/domains. Correlate file-open events (rare, large files) with network spike timing. Monitor for DNS exfiltration: unusually long or base64-encoded DNS queries to external nameservers.

suggestion.title: KVM Guest Memory Boundary Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'guest VMs escape to host'—detection should trigger on memory access patterns crossing VM boundaries. Exploitation requires reading/writing host kernel memory from guest context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when QEMU/KVM processes attempt mmap() or madvise() syscalls with flags that cross EPT (Extended Page Table) boundaries, or when guest vCPU threads access host-owned memory regions. Correlate with abnormal page table walks or TLB flushing patterns not typical of legitimate VM operations.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via KVM Architectural Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 16-year-old Linux KVM flaw on Intel and AMD; indicates exploitation path from guest kernel code to host kernel execution. 'x86 systems' suggests architecture-specific CPU feature abuse (e.g., TSX, EPT misconfiguration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes running in guest context executing privileged CPU instructions or KVM-specific hypercalls not permitted from guest ring level. Flag repeated vmcall invocations with arguments attempting to modify host page tables or CPU registers.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Module Load from Guest-Attributed Process
suggestion.rationale: Successful VM escape implies ability to inject code into host kernel; article's 'lets guest VMs escape to host' suggests eventual host kernel compromise. Detect anomalous module loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insmod() or modprobe operations where parent process is qemu-system-* or within guest namespace, or where memory origin is guest-allocated regions. Flag any kernel module load lacking signed driver certificate when kernel module signing is enforced.

suggestion.title: Host Root Filesystem Access from KVM Guest Thread
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates host compromise once escape succeeds. Post-exploitation, attacker gains access to host /etc, /boot, /root directories. Detect suspicious FS traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file open/read operations targeting host root FS paths (/boot, /etc, /root, /var/log) from qemu or kvm-attributed processes, especially rapid directory enumeration or attempts to read sensitive files (shadow, sudoers, authorized_keys).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of x86 TSX or EPT Side-Channel in KVM
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Intel and AMD x86 systems'; 16-year-old KVM flaw likely leverages hardware-specific CPU features (TSX transactional abort, EPT misconfiguration). Detect architectural exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal TSX_ABORT counts, excessive EPT misses, or patterns of speculative memory reads followed by privileged memory access in KVM vCPU contexts. Flag processes triggering repeated transactional aborts followed by successful privileged memory operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Detected on Exposed SharePoint Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' is explicitly recommended. Vulnerability scanner detection is the first gate for a public-facing application under active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan detection of CVE-2026-45659 on SharePoint Server instances. Correlate with network exposure scanning to confirm internet accessibility. Treat positive findings with federal-deadline urgency (due 2026-07-04).

suggestion.title: Deserialization Attack Exploitation Attempts Against SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'deserialization of untrusted data.' Attackers will send malicious .NET serialized objects to trigger code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to SharePoint for serialized object payloads (BinaryFormatter, DataContractSerializer markers, base64-encoded binary content) targeting deserialization endpoints. Flag requests with suspicious Content-Type or abnormally large payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from SharePoint Worker Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Post-exploitation phase: arbitrary code execution under w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from w3wp.exe (SharePoint worker) or owstimer.exe (timer service), especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or csc.exe without documented maintenance windows. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint spawned processes first.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SharePoint Administration Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article permits 'authorized attacker' code execution; threat actors will likely persist via SharePoint admin credentials or object model calls to add backdoor accounts or malicious features.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint audit logs for unexpected user creation, permission elevation, or feature activation by non-admin service accounts. Flag brute-force attempts against SharePoint admin accounts correlating with exploitation attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Public-Facing Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploit...to execute code over a network' and explicitly maps T1190. Must detect inbound exploitation targeting exposed SharePoint instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous HTTP POST/PUT requests to SharePoint root web, _vti_bin/ paths, and known exploit endpoints. Flag requests with serialized .NET payloads, unusual Content-Encoding, or mismatched User-Agent patterns. Correlate with vulnerability scan results to find exposed SharePoint on external interfaces.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from SharePoint Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute code' via deserialization; successful exploitation spawns child processes from w3wp.exe/SharePoint services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or rundll32.exe spawned by w3wp.exe or SharePoint-related service accounts with unusual command-line arguments, working directory, or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unpatched CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Compliance requires confirmation even on systems reported as patched.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all SharePoint Server instances. Cross-check patch levels against Microsoft security bulletins. Flag gaps between scan date and patch date. Audit systems missing expected KB updates across the fleet.

suggestion.title: Network C2 from Compromised SharePoint Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates authorized remote code execution leads to post-compromise activity; compromised SharePoint services are strategic persistence/lateral-movement pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from SharePoint app-pool and service accounts to external or suspicious internal IP ranges. Flag DNS lookups for known C2 domains, unusual ports (4444, 5555, 8888), or beaconing patterns. Correlate with file writes to temp/ProgramData for staged payloads.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory: Vulnerable SharePoint Server versions (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article states entry is in CISA KEV ('observed exploited in the wild') with mandatory federal remediation by 2026-07-04. Article phrase: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [.../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure].' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference organizational asset inventory against known-vulnerable SharePoint Server versions for CVE-2026-45659. Alert on any unpatched instances where remediation deadline (2026-07-04) has passed, particularly those reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Exploitation detection: Suspicious deserialization payloads to SharePoint endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core vector as 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability which allows authorized attacker to execute code over a network.' Pipeline failed to generate exploitation-phase detection despite this being the active attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint Server w3wp.exe for anomalous HTTP POST requests containing serialized .NET objects targeting SOAP/REST endpoints. Correlate with external or low-reputation source IPs. Detect unusual gadget chains (ObjectDataProvider, WindowsIdentity, etc.) in request payloads before deserialization.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation execution: Unexpected process spawning from SharePoint worker process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability leads to code execution. No detection use case was generated for the execution phase despite RCE being the stated impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal child processes spawned by w3wp.exe (SharePoint IIS worker) such as cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe without corresponding application-level initialization events. Correlate timing with inbound network traffic from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Patch compliance: CVE-2026-45659 remediation status post-deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal deadline 2026-07-04 and states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' No compliance or patch-status detection was generated despite patch verification being the primary mitigation strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management database to flag SharePoint Server instances still running unpatched versions as of deadline date. Escalate findings for environments with internet-facing instances or those serving high-criticality business functions.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Hunt: CVE-2026-45659 SharePoint Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-45659 is in CISA KEV (active exploitation) with federal patch due 2026-07-04; any unpatched instance is directly at-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems to inventory all SharePoint Server instances and flag those not at a patched version for CVE-2026-45659. Prioritize instances with internet exposure.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Deserialization Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes 'deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability'; exploitation payloads will contain binary serialization markers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint HTTP endpoints for requests containing .NET BinaryFormatter headers (AQIDAA) or suspiciously large POST bodies to file handlers (.asmx, web service paths). Cross-correlate with failed authentication or unusual user-agents.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution from SharePoint Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows...execute code over a network'; successful exploitation manifests as child process creation under w3wp.exe or OWSTIMER.EXE with unexpected cmdline or network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by SharePoint worker processes (w3wp.exe, OWSTIMER.EXE) that have not been whitelisted, especially those executing scripts, spawning cmd.exe, or making outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed SharePoint Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: MITRE context notes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; CISA KEV entries target public-facing instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all externally resolvable SharePoint server hostnames via DNS and test network reachability to ports 80, 443, and SharePoint management ports. Cross-correlate unpatched instances with public exposure to triage critical risk.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Diagnostic Log Anomalies During Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation in the wild (CISA KEV); failed and successful deserialization attempts are logged in SharePoint diagnostic logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs (Unified Logging System) for deserialization errors, cryptographic exceptions, or unexpected object instantiation failures that precede successful code execution or process spawning.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-45659 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Execution from SharePoint Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms attackers can 'execute code' post-compromise. Pipeline generated no execution-phase behavioral detection for spawned processes under compromised service account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned by SharePoint worker processes (w3wp.exe, owstimer.exe). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, whoami from service account context. Correlate with recent HTTP requests to SharePoint endpoints to establish causal link.

suggestion.title: Internet-Routable SharePoint Server Exposure Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 'public-facing application'; body directs 'asset-exposure hunt' as canonical response. Pipeline omitted exposure detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all SharePoint Server instances reachable from internet-routable address space. Cross-reference patch status for CVE-2026-45659. Flag any unpatched SharePoint servers. Correlate with external threat-intel for active scanning/probing activity targeting SharePoint.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication to Successful Exploitation Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'authorized attacker' implies credential compromise pathway. Pipeline missed initial access chain showing failed auth attempts preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of HTTP 401/403 responses to SharePoint endpoints from external IP, followed by successful authenticated requests. Flag if credentials used belong to service account or disabled user—indicates takeover.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Compromised public-facing SharePoint becomes network pivot; article states 'execute code over a network.' Pipeline missed lateral movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SharePoint server to internal infrastructure (DC, file servers, SQL). Alert if spawned from non-standard service process. Correlate process creation events on same host with code execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: SharePoint Server Public Exposure Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can exploit 'over a network' and CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation in the wild. Network-accessible SharePoint instances are the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for SharePoint services on standard ports (443, 80, 8080) and alternate HTTP/S ports. Correlate vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-45659 with network accessibility logs. Alert on unpatched instances after federal due date 2026-07-04.

suggestion.title: Deserialization Payload Detection in SharePoint Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'deserialization of untrusted data' as the vulnerability mechanism. Exploitation requires sending malicious serialized objects; these appear as anomalous request bodies to SharePoint endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to SharePoint webservices and _api endpoints for base64-encoded or binary serialized .NET object signatures (System.Runtime.Serialization markers, CLR payload indicators). Alert on abnormal request entropy or size to vulnerable SharePoint paths.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from SharePoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows code execution'; successful exploitation manifests as command spawning. SharePoint processes (w3wp.exe, owstimer.exe) normally do not launch cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or non-system interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, csc.exe, or net.exe spawned as children of w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe without corresponding SharePoint administrative action. Monitor for unsigned or suspicious dlls loaded by SharePoint processes post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from SharePoint Application
suggestion.rationale: Post-execution, attacker code running in SharePoint context may establish C2 or stage secondary payloads. Outbound network activity from SharePoint processes is anomalous outside normal replication/federation scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from w3wp.exe or owstimer.exe to non-internal hosts, especially on ports 443, 8080, or high-numbered ports. Alert on DNS queries initiated by SharePoint processes to external or recently-registered domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Federal civilian agencies required to patch by 2026-07-04. Any unpatched SharePoint instance post-deadline remains exposed to documented active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scans weekly post-due-date against all SharePoint Server instances. Generate daily alerts for non-compliant systems. Cross-reference unpatched, network-exposed instances for immediate remediation priority.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed or Exploited SharePoint Deserialization (CVE-2026-45659)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE is 'actively exploited in the wild' and lists it in CISA KEV; recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.' Pipeline produced no UC despite explicit guidance to hunt for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound requests to SharePoint Server on ports 80/443 with payloads indicative of deserialization exploit attempts (e.g., base64-encoded .NET objects, unusual binary content-type). Correlate with failed authentication or anomalous request patterns. Baseline normal SharePoint traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Monitor Abnormal Process Execution from SharePoint Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authorized attacker to execute code over a network' — implies post-exploitation code execution. No UC for detecting unusual child processes, network connections, or file activity spawned by SharePoint services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from SharePoint worker processes (w3wp.exe, spoolsv.exe under SharePoint context) — particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or net.exe. Monitor for outbound network connections from SharePoint PIDs. Establish baseline of legitimate SharePoint child processes and hunt deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious .NET Deserialization Events
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'deserialization of untrusted data' — article emphasizes this as the attack vector. No UC for detecting abnormal deserialization, gadget chain loading, or unsafe reflection in SharePoint context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for .NET runtime warnings/errors related to deserialization, unsafe reflection, or serialization gadget chains in event logs (keywords: BinaryFormatter, ObjectInputStream, TypeConfusedDelegate). Cross-reference with SharePoint process context and unusual assembly loads.

suggestion.title: Track CVE-2026-45659 Patch Compliance Against Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-04' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline missed compliance/asset-inventory UC entirely despite explicit deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output and patch management logs to inventory all SharePoint Server instances, flag unpatched hosts, and correlate against patch-deployment logs. Generate compliance report showing time-to-remediation vs. federal deadline; escalate any > 14 days past due.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized SharePoint Administrative Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'authorized attacker' but realistic scenario includes compromise of legitimate credentials, leading to administrative object manipulation. No UC for detecting anomalous SharePoint admin operations (site creation, user addition, permission changes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SharePoint ULS logs and audit trails for anomalous admin actions: new site collections, hidden sites, user group additions, permission escalations, content deployment. Baseline expected admin behavior and flag after-hours or unusual-account administrative activity.
